sourceDefinition: , (S Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. dalokN , (S, Msb,) He rubbed it, or rubbed it and pressed it, (M, Msb, K,) with his hand: (S, M, Msb, K:) [or he did so well: or he pressed it, or squeezed it, and rubbed it: for] dalokN signifies the act of rubbing, or rubbing and pressing, well: (KL:) or the act of pressing, or squeezing, and rubbing: (Ham p. 798:) [and in like manner, ↓ dl~khu , inf. n. tadoliykN , signifies in the present day he rubbed it, or rubbed it and pressed it; and particularly, a person's body and limbs, in the bath: its proper meaning, however, is, he rubbed it, or rubbed it and pressed it, much or well: Golius explains it as signifying he rubbed it much or well on the anthority of the KL; but it is not in my copy of that work.] You say, dalaka Alv~awoba He rubbed, or rubbed and pressed, the garment, or piece of cloth, to wash it. (TA.) And dalakotu Als~unobula Hat~aY A@nofaraka qi$oruhu Eano Hab~ihi [ I rubbed the ears of corn until their husks rubbed off from their grain ]; (TA;) and ↓ Aid~alakahu [signifies the same]. (K in art. rhw , &c.) And dalaka Eayonayohi [ He rubbed his eyes ]; i. e., a man looking at the setting sun. (Z, TA.) And dalakati AlmaroA^apu AlEajiyna [ The woman kneaded the dough ]. (TA.) And dalakotu Aln~aEola biAlA^aroDi I wiped the sandal with [meaning upon ] the ground. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] dalakahu Ald~ahoru (tropical:) Time, or fortune, disciplined him well, tried, or proved, him, rendered him expert, or experienced, or firm or sound in judgment, and taught him. (K,* TA.) And dalakatohu AlA^asofaAru (tropical:) Journeyings inured him to them; namely, a camel. (TA.) And dulika biAlA^asofaAri , said of a camel, (A, O, L, K,) (tropical:) He was inured by journeyings, and habituated thereto: (A, L:) or he was fatigued, or jaded, by journeyings; like [ duk~a and] kud~a . (O, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] dulikati AlA^aroDu (assumed tropical:) [ The produce, or herbage, of ] the land was eaten, or consumed. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- See also 3. -A2- dalakati Al$~amosu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. duluwkN , (S, Mgh, &c.,) (tropical:) The sun set; (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.;) accord. to Z, because he who looks at it rubs ( yadoluku ) his eyes, so that it is as though it were the rubber; (TA;) and in like manner, Aln~ujuwmu the stars: (Msb:) or became yellow, (K, TA,) and inclined to setting: (TA:) or declined (K, * TA) so that the beholder almost required, when looking at it, to contract the rays from his eyes with the palm of his hand: (TA:) or declined after midday: (Ibn-'Omar, TA:) or it signifies (or signifies also, Msb) the sun declined from the meridian, or midheaven, (I'Ab, Fr, Zj, Az, S, * Mgh, * Msb, K, &c.,) at noon; (I'Ab, Fr, Zj, Az;) and in like manner, Aln~ujuwmu the stars. (Msb.) sourceDefinition: , (aor. tu*aAr~u , S,) inf. n. mu*aAr~apN and *iraArN , She (a camel) became evil in her disposition. (Fr, S, K.) Hence the saying of Hoteiäh, satirizing Ez-Zibrikán, and praising the family of Shemmás Ibn-Láy, wakunota ka*aAti Albaw~i *aArato biA^anofihaA famino *aAka tabogiY buEodahu watuhaAjiruho i. e. [ And thou wast like her who has a stuffed skin of a young camel made for her and placed near her that she may incline to it and yield her milk, ] that has inclined to the young one of another; [ and on that account desires its distance from her, and severs herself from it: ] in the S we find, for Albaw~i , AlbaEoli ; and for buEodahu , gayorahu ; but the former are the correct readings: *aArato is a contraction of *aAr~ato : or, accord. to some, it is for *aA='arato : see art. *A^r . (IB and TA.) ― -b2- One says also, fiY fulaAnK *iraArN , meaning (assumed tropical:) In such a one is aversion, arising from anger, like that of a she-camel: (AZ, S:) or anger and aversion (Th, M, K, TA) and disapprobation. (Th, TA)

sourceDefinition: , [aor. ,] inf. n. *ikoraY , (S, A, Msb,) which is fem., (Msb,) and imperfectly decl., (S,) and *ikorN (A, K) [and *ukorN , or, accord. to EtTebreezee, (Ham p. 26,) the latter of these two but not the former, or, as is said in the Msb., both are properly substs., and a distinction is made between them, as will be shown below,] and ta*okaArN , (K,) He preserved it in his memory: (K, * TA:) he remembered it; (S, A;) as also *akarahu biqalobihi [to distinguish it from *akara in a sense afterwards to be explained], (S, Msb,) and ↓ t*k~rhu ; (S, A;) and ↓ Aid~akarahu (S, K, TA,) originally Ai*otakarahu (S,) and Ai*~akarahu (TA, and so in the CK,) and Ai*odakarahu (K,) and ↓ Ast*krhu , (AZ, K,) signify the same as t*k~rhu (K) [as explained above]: ↓ t*k~rhu signifies also he became reminded of it; (Msb;) [and so ↓ Ad~krhu and its variations: and ↓ Ast*krhu seems properly to signify, as also ↓ t*kr~hu , he recollected it; or called it to mind: and he sought to remember it: and ↓ Ast*kr and ↓ t*k~r used intransitively, he sought, or endeavoured, to remember. ] You say, *akarotu Al$~aYo'a baEoda Aln~isoyaAni [ I remembered the thing after forgetting ]: (S:) and *akarotu AlmanosiY~a and ↓ ta*ak~arotuhu [ I remembered the thing forgotten, and I became reminded of it, or I recollected it ]: (A:) and baEoda A^amahK ↓ Ad~kr , occurring in the Kur [xii. 45, accord. to one reading of the last word], means He remembered [or became reminded ] after forgetting. (S) And rabaTa fiY bihi HaAjatihi ↓ A_iSobaEihi xayoTFA yasota*okiru [ He tied upon his finger a thread or string, seeking to remember, or recollect, or call to mind, thereby the thing that he wanted: such a thread or string is commonly called ratiymapN :]: (AZ:) and ↓ Ast*kr is used alone with the like signification [i. e. He sought to remember ]: and also signifies He studied a book and preserved it in his memory, accord. to the K; but accord. to other lexicons, he studied a thing in order to remember it, or preserve it in his memory: (TA:) you say, bidiraAsatihi ↓ Ast*kr He sought to remember by his studying of a book. sourceDefinition: (Yoo, A'Obeyd, Yaakoob, S, M, A, Msb, K) and ↓ *ukorN , (Yoo, A'Obeyd, Yaakoob, S, A, Msb, K, TA,) or the latter only in the first of the senses here to be explained, (Fr, Msb, TA,) and the latter only is mentioned in this sense in the Fs, (TA,) and is said by El-Ahmar to be of the dial. of Kureysh, (TA,) [both said in the Msb to be simple substs., though many hold them to be inf. ns.,] and ↓ *akorN , accord. to one of the expositors of the Fs, but this is strange, (TA,) and ↓ *ikorapN (S, M) and ↓ *ukorapN (M, TA) and ↓ *ikoraY , (S, M, [see 1, first sentence,]) and also dikorN (S) and dukorN , mentioned by ISd as of the dial. of Rabee'ah, but held by him to be of weak authority, (TA,) Remembrance; (S, M, A, Msb, K, &c.;) the presence of a thing in the mind: (Er-Rághib:) also termed *ikorN biAlqalobi , (Msb, TA,) to distinguish it from *ikorN in another sense, to be explained below: (TA:) he pl. of ↓ *ikorapN is *ikarN , (M,) also said to be pl. of ↓ *ikoraY . (MF, art. AHd .) You say, ↓ AijoEalohu minoka EalaY *ukorK and *ikorK in the same sense, Place thou him, or it, in thy remembrance. (S.) And A^ajoEalahu min~iY ↓ EalaY *ukorK , and *ikorK , I will not forget him, or it. (A.) And ↓ maA zaAla min~iY EalaY *ukorK , and *ikorK (K,) or the former only, (Fr, Msb, TA,) He, or it, did not cease to be in my remembrance; (K;) I did not forget him, or it. (Fr, TA.) And ↓ A^anota min~iY EalaY *ukorK Thou art in my mind. (ISd, Lb.) ― -b2- The words in the Kur [xxix. 44] wala*ikoru A@ll~`hi A^akobaru admit of two explanations: The remembrance of God is better for a man than a man's remembrance of a man: and the remembrance of God is better as more efficacious in forbidding evil conduct than is prayer. (TA.) ― -b3- *ikorN also signifies Memory; a certain quality of the mind, by which a man is able to remember what he cares to know; like HifuZN , except that this latter term is used with regard to the preservation of a thing [in the mind], whereas the former is used with regard to calling it to mind. (Er-Rághib.) -A2- Also *ikorN (Er-Rághib, Msb, TA) and ↓ *ukorN , (Msb, TA,) or the former only accord. to Fr, (Msb, TA,) and ↓ *ikoraY (Msb,) The mention, telling, relating, or saying, of a thing: said by some to be contr. of SamotN : (TA:) and also termed *ikorN biAll~isaAni (Msb, TA,) to distinguish it from *ikorN in the sense first explained above. (TA.) ― -b2- Also *ikorN (assumed tropical:) The praise, and glorification, of God; the celebration, or declaration, of his remoteness, or freedom, from every impurity or imperfection, or from everything derogatory from his glory; or the saying suboHaAna , A@ll~`hi , [ and AlHamodu lil~`hi , and A^all~`hu A^akobaru ,] and laA A_ilaAha A_il~aA A@ll~`hu , [&c., see 1,] and uttering all the forms of his praise: a reading, or reciting, of the Kur-án: a thanking [ God ]: obedience [ to God ]: (Abu-l- 'Abbás:) prayer to God; (K;) supplication. (Abu-l-'Abbás, K.) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) Praise, or eulogy, or good speech, of another. (S, * K, * TA.) ― -b4- [And, accord. to some, (tropical:) Dispraise, or evil speech. See 1.] ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) A thing that is current upon the tongue. (K.) ― -b6- (tropical:) Fame; renown; report; reputation; (S, A, K;) whether good or evil; (ISd;) as also ↓ *ukorapN . (AZ, ISd, K.) Thus in the saying, lahu *ikorN fiY Aln~aAsi (tropical:) He has fame among the people: in which it has also the signification next following. (A.) ― -b7- (tropical:) Eminence; nobility; honour. (S, A, Msb, K.) So in the Kur [xciv. 4], warafaEonaA laka *ikoraka (tropical:) And We have raised for thee thine eminence, or thy nobility, or thine honour: as some say, it means, when I am mentioned, thou art mentioned with Me: and again, in the Kur [xliii. 43], wa A_in~ahu la*ikorN laka wa liqawomika (tropical:) And verily it (the Kur-án) is an honour to thee and to thy people. (TA.) Also, in the Kur [xxxviii. 1], wa AlquroA=ni *iY Al*~ikori (tropical:) By the Kur-án possessed of eminence, &c. (S) ― -b8- Also (assumed tropical:) A book containing an exposition of religion, and an institution of religious laws: (K:) any book of the prophets: (TA:) and especially the Kur-án: (MF, TA:) and the taworaApN [or Book of the Law revealed to Moses ]: (Aboo-Hureyreh, TA in art. zbr :) and that [ law ] which is [ recorded ] in heaven. (Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr, TA ubi suprà.) ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) An exhortation; an admonition, or a warning. (Bd in xxxviii. 1.) ― -b10- *ikoru Haq~K (tropical:) A written obligation; syn. Sak~N : (A, K:) pl. *ukuwru Haq~K , (A,) or *ukuwru HuquwqK . (TA.) You say, liY EalaY h`*aA AlA^amori *ikoru Haq~K (tropical:) [ I have a written obligation to insure this thing ]. (A.) -A3- See also the next paragraph, in the latter half.

definition: [probably originally signifying “ mentioned, ” or “ talked of, ” of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , like nafaDN in the sense of manofuwDN , and xabaTN in the sense of maxobuwTN , and qabaDN in the sense of maqobuwDN , &c.
sourceDefinition: [probably originally signifying “ mentioned, ” or “ talked of, ” of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , like nafaDN in the sense of manofuwDN , and xabaTN in the sense of maxobuwTN , and qabaDN in the sense of maqobuwDN , &c.; and hence the first, and perhaps most others, of the significations here following:] Male; masculine; of the male, or masculine, sex, or gender; contr. of A^unovaY : (S, A, Msb, K, &c.:) [the corresponding word in Hebrew ( ) has been supposed to have this signification because a male is much “ mentioned, ” or “ talked of; ” and it is well known that the Arabs make comparatively little account of a female:] pl. *ukuwrN (S, A, Msb, K) and *ukuwrapN (A, Msb, K) and *ikaArN (K) and *ikaArapN and *ukoraAnN (S, A, Msb, K) and *ikarapN : (S, K:) [the last, in one copy of the S, I find written ↓ *ikorapN , which, if correct, is a pl. of pauc.: and in the TA, in the same phrase in which it occurs in the S, it is written ↓ *ukorapN , and expressly said to be with damm, so that it is a quasi-pl. n.:] the pl. form with w and n is not allowable. (Msb.) One says, kami Al*~ikarapu mino waladika , or ↓ Al*~ikorapu , (accord. to different copies of the S,) or ↓ Al*~ukorapu , with damm, (accord. to the TA,) How many are the males of thy children? (S, TA.) ― -b2- The male organ of generation; the penis; syn. EawofN ; (S, K, &c.;) of a man: (TA:) or the faroj [an equivocal term, but here evidently used in the above-mentioned sense,] of an animal: (Msb:) pl. *ukuwrN , (K,) or *ikarapN , like EinabapN , (Msb,) or *ikaArapN , (T, TA,) and ↓ ma*aAkiyru : (S, Msb, K:) the last contr. to analogy, (S, Msb,) as though used for the sake of distinction between this signification and the one immediately preceding: (S:) or of the same class as maHaAsinu [with respect to HusonN ] and malaAmiHu [with respect to lamoHapN ]: (ISd:) Akh says that it is a pl. without a [proper] sing., like EabaAbiydu and A^abaAbiylu : accord. to the T, it has no sing.; or if it have a sing., it is ↓ mu*okirN , like muqodimN , of which the pl. is maqaAdiymu ; and signifies the parts next to the penis: (TA:) or it signifies the penis with what is around it; [or the genitals; ] and is similar to mafaAriqu in the phrase $aAbato mafaAriqu raA^osihi : and qaTaEa ma*aAkiyrahu signified He extirpated his penis. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Applied to a man, (A, K,) it also signifies (tropical:) Strong; courageous; acute and ardent; vigorous and effective in affairs; [and also] stubborn; and disdainful: (TA:) or [ masculine, meaning] perfect; like as A^unovaY is applied to a woman. (T and A in art. Anv .) The signification of “ strong, courageous, and stubborn, ” and the significations which the same word has when applied to rain and to a saying, are assigned in the K to ↓ *ikorN ; but [SM says,] I know not how this is; for in the other lexicons they are assigned to *akarN . (TA.) You say, laA yafoEaluhu A_il~aA *ukuwrapu Alr~ijaAli (tropical:) [ None will do it but such as are strong, &c., of men ]. (A.) ― -b4- Applied to iron, (tropical:) Of the toughest and best quality, (K,) and strongest; (TA;) contr. of A^aniyvN ; (S;) [iron converted into steel; ] as also ↓ *akiyrN . (K.) [See also *ukorapN .] ― -b5- Applied to a sword, (tropical:) Having maA=' [i. e., diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain ]; (S;) as also ↓ mu*~ak~arN : (S, K:) or of which the edge is of steel ( HadiydN *akarN ) and the maton [or middle of the broad side ] of soft iron; of which the people say that they are of the fabric of the Jinn, or Genii: (A'Obeyd, S:) or ↓ mu*ak~aru signifies having a sharp iron blade or edge: (As:) the pl. of the former is *ukuwrN . (Ham p. 168.) ― -b6- *ukuwru Albuquwli (tropical:) Herbs, or leguminous plants, that are hard and thick: (TA voce Eu$obN :) or that are thick, and inclining to bitterness: (S, TA:) like as A^aHoraAruhaA signifies such as are slender and sweet: (TA:) or the former signifies such as are thick and rough. (AHeyth.) ― -b7- *ukuwrapu AlT~iybi , (K,) and *ukuwruhu , and *ikaAratuhu , (TA,) (tropical:) Perfume proper for men, exclusively of women: i. e., (TA,) that leaves no stain; (K, * TA;) that becomes dissipated; such as musk, and aloes-wood, and camphire, and gaAliyap , and *ariyrap . (TA.) [See the contr., TiybN muw^an~avN , in art. Anv .] ― -b8- *akarN applied to the Kur-án signifies (tropical:) Eminently excellent. (K.) See 2. ― -b9- Applied to a saying, (tropical:) Strong and firm: and in like manner to poetry. (A.) ― -b10- The Arabs disliked a she-camel's bringing forth a male; and hence they applied the term *akarN , met., to (tropical:) Anything disliked. (A.) ― -b11- [Thus,] applied to rain, it signifies (tropical:) Violent; (A, K;) falling in large drops. (K.) They said, A^aSaAbati AlA^aroDa *ukuwru AlA^asomiyapi (tropical:) Rains bringing intense cold and torrents fell upon the earth. (A.) ― -b12- Applied to a day, (tropical:) [ Severe; distressing; hard to be borne: see also mu*ak~arN ]. (A.) ― -b13- IDrd says, I think that the name Al*kr [so in the TA, without any syll. signs; app. Al*~akaru ] is applied by some of the Arabs to Als~imaAku Alr~aAmiHu [or the star Arcturus ]. (TA.)

[See also *ukorapN .] ― -b5- Applied to a sword, (tropical:) Having maA=' [i. e., diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain ]; (S;) as also ↓ mu*~ak~arN : (S, K:) or of which the edge is of steel ( HadiydN *akarN ) and the maton [or middle of the broad side ] of soft iron; of which the people say that they are of the fabric of the Jinn, or Genii: (A'Obeyd, S:) or ↓ mu*ak~aru signifies having a sharp iron blade or edge: (As:) the pl. of the former is *ukuwrN . (Ham p. 168.) ― -b6- *ukuwru Albuquwli (tropical:) Herbs, or leguminous plants, that are hard and thick: (TA voce Eu$obN :) or that are thick, and inclining to bitterness: (S, TA:) like as A^aHoraAruhaA signifies such as are slender and sweet: (TA:) or the former signifies such as are thick and rough. (A.) ― -b10- The Arabs disliked a she-camel's bringing forth a male; and hence they applied the term *akarN , met., to (tropical:) Anything disliked. (A.) ― -b11- [Thus,] applied to rain, it signifies (tropical:) Violent; (A, K;) falling in large drops. (K.) They said, A^aSaAbati AlA^aroDa *ukuwru AlA^asomiyapi (tropical:) Rains bringing intense cold and torrents fell upon the earth. (A.) ― -b13- IDrd says, I think that the name Al*kr [so in the TA, without any syll. signs; app. Al*~akaru ] is applied by some of the Arabs to Als~imaAku Alr~aAmiHu [or the star Arcturus ]. (TA.)

definition: A vitiousness, or an impediment, in speech or utterance, so that one does not speak distinctly: (S, A, K:) or a hastiness therein, (M, Mgh,) and a want of distinctness: or the changing of l into Y :...

definition: , (S, M, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, K,) aor. , (M, K,) inf. n. ravo'N , (S, M,) He drew milk from the udder upon sour milk, so that it thickened, (S, K,) and became what is termed raviyoy^ap : (K:) or he mixed fresh milk with sour milk: or, as some say, he made milk to become what is termed raviyoy^ap : (M:) or it has this last signification, and also signifies he mixed [ in an absolute sense ]. (K.) [Az says,] I heard an Arab of the desert, of Benoo-Mudarris, say to a servant of his, AirovaA^o liY lubayonapF A^a$orabuhaA [ Mix thou for me a little milk so as to make raviyoy^ap , which I will drink ]. (T.) And you say, ravaA^a Alqawoma (M, K) and ravaA^a lahumo (M) He made for the party raviyoy^ap . (M, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] humo yarovaw^uwna raA^oyahumo , (S,) and ravaw^uwA raA^oyahumo , (M,) inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) They confuse, or confound, and they confused, or confounded, their judgment, or opinion. (S, M. [See also 8.]) ― -b3- And [hence also, perhaps, as rvyy^p is said to be beaten with a mijodaH in the mixing of it,] He beat (K) with a staff, or stick. (TA.) -A2- It (anger) became stilled, or appeased. (K.) -A3- He (a camel) became affected with the disease termed ravoA^ap . (K.) -A4- Also, (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (M,) a dial. var. of ravaY , meaning He eulogized a man after his death [ in verse or otherwise; or he wept for him, or over him, enumerating his good qualities or actions ]: (M, K: *) and in like manner one says of a woman eulogizing her husband after his death; inf. n. maroviy^apN : (M:) ISk mentions an Arab woman's saying ravaA^otu zawojiY biA^aboyaAtK [ I eulogized my husband after his death with verses ]; pronouncing the verb with ' ; but it is originally without ' : (S, Sgh:) Fr says that her doing this arose from her finding them to say ravaA^otu All~abana and her therefore supposing Almaroviyap to be from the same source: (TA in the present art.:) or, accord. to Fr, their chasteness of speech sometimes induced them to pronounce with ' that which is [properly] without ' ; and thus they said ravaA^otu Almay~ita and lab~aA^otu biAlHaj~i and Hal~aA^otu Als~awiyqa . (TA in art. rvw .)

definition: Sour milk upon which fresh milk is drawn from the udder, so that it becomes thick: (Lh, S, M, K:) or fresh milk poured upon sour, (As, T, M, Mgh,) and then stirred about with a [ wooden instrument...
sourceDefinition: Sour milk upon which fresh milk is drawn from the udder, so that it becomes thick: (Lh, S, M, K:) or fresh milk poured upon sour, (As, T, M, Mgh,) and then stirred about with a [ wooden instrument called ] mijodaH until it becomes thick: (Lh, M:) or fresh milk upon which sour milk is poured, then left a while, whereupon thin yellow water [or whey ] comes forth, and is poured away from it, and then the thick is drunk. (Har p. 451.) One says, Alr~aviyoy^apu tafovaA^u AlgaDaba (S, TA) What is termed rvyy^p stills, or appeases, anger: (TA:) alluding to [the effect produced by] a small kindness: a saying which originated from a man's being incensed against some persons. and being hungry, and their giving him to drink some rvyy^p , whereupon his anger became appeased: (S in art. fvA^ :) hence it became a proverb. (TA.) -A2- See also ravoA^apN .

definition: Spreading, (Lth, TA,) or widely expanded;
sourceDefinition: Spreading, (Lth, TA,) or widely expanded; (TA;) applied to a solid hoof, (Lth, TA,) and to a foot such as is termed xuf~ : (TA:) and wide; applied to anything: thus qadamN raH~aA='u a wide human foot: (Lth, TA:) and a human foot having the middle of the sole even with the fore part; (L, TA;) flat-soled; i. e. having, in the sole, no hollow part that does not touch the ground: (S:) and kirokir~pN raH~aA='u a wide callous protuberance upon the breast of a camel: (TA:) and jafonapN raH~aA='u a wide [ bowl such as is termed ] jifnp ; like rawoHaA='u ; wide and not deep: (TA:) and jifaAnN ruHuHN wide jfAn [pl. of jafonapN ]. (IAar, K.) Having a spreading hoof; (S, A, K;) applied to a horse, (A,) and to a mountain-goat: (S, A, K:) also, applied to a man, having a wide foot; (A;) or having, in the sole of his foot, no hollow part that does not touch the ground, (S, K,) as is the case in the feet of the Zinj; (S;) having the sole of the foot flat, so that all of it touches the ground: fem. raH~aA='u : you say AimoraA^apN raH~aA='u Alqadamayoni : a high hollow to the sole of the foot is approved in a man and in a woman. (T, TA.) Also, applied to a camel, Having one foot cleaving to another. (TA.)

definition: , (S, M, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, M, L,) inf. n. rad~N (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and marad~N (S, M, L, K) and maroduwdN , (S, L, K,) this last an inf. n. like maHoluwfN and maEoquwlN , (S, L,) and rid~apN (S [there said to be an inf. n., like rad~N of rad~ahu , aor. ,]) and rid~iydaY , (S, L, K, [but in the S and L merely said to be syn. with rad~N ,]) an intensive form, (Mgh, TA,) and tarodaAdN , which is [also] an intensive or a frequentative inf. n. of rad~ahu , (Sb, M, L,) and likewise an inf. n. of rd~dhu ; (Sb, S, M, L;) and ↓ Artd~hu ; (M, L;) He made, or caused, him, or it, to return, go back, come back, or revert; sent, turned, or put, him, or it, back, or away; returned, rejected, repelled, or averted, him, or it; syn. rajaEahu , (S, M, L, Msb,) and Sarafahu , (S, M, L, K) and dafaEahu ; (Msb in art. dfE , &c.;) Eano wajohihi [ from his, or its, course ]. (S, M.) Hence, in the Kur [xxx. 42 and xlii. 46], yawomN laA marad~a lahu [ A day which there shall be no repelling, or averting ], meaning the day of resurrection. (Th, M, L.) One says, A^amoru A@ll~`hi laA marad~a lahu The command of God, there is no repelling, or averting it. (L.) And layosa liA^amori A@ll~`hi maroduwdN i. e. rad~N [ There is no repelling, or averting, the command of God. ] (A.) And rad~ahu Eani AlA^amori He made him to return or revert, or turned him back or away, with gentleness, from the thing, or affair; as also lad~ahu . (T, L.) ― -b2- Accord. to some, rad~a is made doubly trans. with A_ilaY to the second objective complement when honour is intended to be shown, and with EalaY when dishonour is intended; and they adduce as evidence of the correctness of their assertion the sayings in the Kur [xxviii. 12] faradadonaAhu A_ilaY A^um~ihi [ So we returned, or restored, him to his mother ] and [iii. 142] yarud~uwkumo EalaY A^aEoqaAbikumo [ They will turn you back, or cause you to return, to your former condition ]: but instances may be found at variance with this assertion. (MF.) [Such instances are of frequent occurrence; though in others, the distinction pointed out above is observed, as may be seen in what here follows.] You say, rad~ahu A_ilaY manozilihi He sent him back to his abode. (S, L, Msb.) And rad~a A_ilayohi jawaAbFA He returned, or rendered, to him a reply, or an answer; (S, A, * L, Msb;) he sent to him a reply, or an answer. (Msb.) And rad~a Ealayohi He replied to him, or answered him, in an absolute sense; (L;) and also, by way of refutation or objection, i. e. he replied against him; faqaAla and said, or biqawolihi by his saying. (TA &c., passim.) And rad~a Ealayohi Als~alaAma He returned to him the salutation. (The Trads. &c., passim.) And rad~a Ealayohi AlwadiyEapa He returned, rendered, restored, or sent [ back ], to him the deposite; (Msb;) and AlmaniyHapa [ the she-camel, or sheep, or goat, lent to him for him to milk her ]. (S in art. mnH .) And rad~a Ealayohi Al$~aYo'a , (S, Mgh, L, K,) inf. n. rad~N and marad~N , (Mgh,) He rejected the thing, (such as a gift, A, and bad money, L,) refusing to receive it, or accept it, from him; [ as though he cast it back at him; ] and so Al$~aYo'a ↓ raAd~ahu . (S, L, K. *) And in like manner, He rejected the thing in reply to him, charging him with error in respect of it. (S, L, K.) And radadotu Ealayohi qawolahu [ I rebutted, rejected, or repudiated, in reply to him, his saying, charging him with error therein; I refused him my assent to it ]. (A, Msb.) [And radadotu qawolahu I rebutted, rejected, or repudiated, in reply, or replication, his saying, as wrong, or erroneous; refuted it, or refelled it; refused assent to it; controverted it, or contradicted it. And rad~a AlA^amora He refused assent, or consent, to the thing, or affair. And rad~a Ealayohi AlA^amora He refused him his assent, or consent, to the thing, or affair. ] And rad~a Als~aAy^ila He turned back, or away, the beggar, or asker, from the object of his want: (A:) [ he rebuffed him: ] or he sent away, or dismissed, the beggar, or asker, either with refusal or with a gift: occurring in trads. with both of these meanings. (L.) ― -b3- rad~a AlbaAba He shut, or closed, the door. (Mgh. [See maroduwdN .]) ― -b4- [ rad~a yadahu A_ilaY sayofihi is a phrase of frequent occurrence, meaning He put back his hand to his sword; it being hung behind him: (see 4 in art. xlf :) and hence, simply, he put his hand to his sword. ] farad~uwA A^ayodiyahumo fiY A^afowaAhihimo , in the Kur xiv. 10, means And they put their hands to their mouths by reason of vehement anger or wrath or rage. (Jel.) ― -b5- rad~ahu fiY A^amorK [ He made him to enter again into an affair, or a state ]. (ISh, TA in art. nks .) ― -b6- rad~a Al$~aYo'a He repeated the thing; did it again; syn. A^aEaAdahu . (M in art. Ewd .) You say, rad~a Ealayohimu AlA^ayomaAna He repeated to them the oaths. (L in art. jld .) [In this sense, rid~iydaY is one of the inf. ns. in use; as in the following ex.] It is said in a trad., laA rid~iydaY fiY AlS~adaqapi [ There shall be no repeating in the case of the poor-rate ]; (T, S, L;) meaning that the poor-rate shall not be taken twice (T, L) in one year. (L.) [See also 2, which has a similar signification.] ― -b7- h`*aA laA yarud~u Ealayoka , originally laA yarud~u Ealayoka $ayoy^FA (assumed tropical:) [ This will not return anything to thee ], means [ this will not bring any return to thee, or] this will not profit thee: (Har p. 483:) and maA yarud~u Ealayoka h`*aA (tropical:) This does not profit thee. (A.) ― -b8- rad~a A_ilayohi AlA^amora (assumed tropical:) [ He referred the affair, or case, to him for management or decision: or] he committed to him the affair, or case; syn. faw~aDahu A_ilayohi . (S and A and K in art. fwD .) ― -b9- [ rad~a Al$~aYo'a A_ilaY A^aSolihi , a phrase of frequent occurrence, He reduced the thing to its original state. ] And rad~a Alr~uboEa xumosFA [ He reduced the fourth part to a fifth part ]. (K in art. rbE .) ― -b10- rad~a A@ll~`hu nafosiY A_ilaY waqoti A@notihaA='i mud~atiY [ God brought my soul to the time of the end of my duration ]. (IB, TA in art. Amr .) ― -b11- rad~ahu A_ilaY AlA^amori [ He reduced him to the thing, or affair ]: (M and K in art. qSr , in explanation of qaSarahu EalaY AlA^amori :) or he appropriated him [or it, restrictively, ] to the thing, or affair. (TK in that art.) ― -b12- rad~a A=xira Al$~aYo'i A_ilaY A^aw~alihi , (S and K in art. Eks , &c,) and rad~a A^aw~alahu EalaY A=xirihi , (Msb in the same art., &c.,) [ He reversed the thing; made the last part of it to be first, and the first part of it to be last; turned it hind part before, and fore part behind. ] And rad~a baEoDa AlA^amori EalaY baEoDi [ He reversed the order of part, or of the parts, of the affair, or case ]. (TA in art. rk .) And radadotu Ealayohi A^amorahu i. q. Eakasotuhu Ealayohi [ I reversed to him his affair, or case; I made his affair, or case, to become the contrary of what it was to him ]. (Msb in art. Eks .) [Hence,] vum~a radadonaA lakumu Alkar~apa Ealayohimo , in the Kur xvii. 6, means [ Then we gave to you ] the turn to prevail against them, or the victory over them. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b13- [Hence, also, rad~ahu sometimes signifies He, or it, rendered him, or it; or caused him, or it, to become; (like Say~arahu ;) when it has a second objective complement the contrary in meaning to the first; as in the following ex.; and it may have this meaning likewise when it has a second objective complement differing in meaning from the first in a less degree.] A poet says, ramaY AlHadavaAnu nisowapa A=li HarobK biA^amorK qado samadona lahu sumuwdaA farad~a $uEuwrahun~a Als~uwda biyDFA warad~a wujuwhahun~a AlbiyDa suwdaA [ The casualties of fortune smote the women of the family of Harb with an event whereat they became confounded with great confoundedness; and it rendered their black hairs white, and rendered their white faces black ]. (L in art. smd .)

sourceDefinition: She (a sheep or goat or other animal) secreted milk in her udder a little before her bringing forth; syn. A^aDoraEato : (S:) [or,] said of a camel, her udder became shining, and infused with milk. (M, L.) And She (a camel) had her udder and vulva inflated, or swollen, in consequence of her lying upon moist ground: or had her vulva swollen in consequence of lust for the stallion: or had her A^arofaAg [or groins, or inguinal creases, or the like ], or her udder, and her vulva, swollen in consequence of drinking much water. (M, L.) [See also murd~N .] ― -b2- And Ard~ [said of a man, app. from the verb as explained in the first sentence of this paragraph, His seminal fluid returned into his back, or he secreted much seminal fluid, in consequence of his having been long without a wife, or absent from his home: see murid~N : and see also 6. And hence, (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, very libidinous: see, again, murid~N . And] (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, swollen with anger. (M. [In the L and TA, erroneously written, in this sense, ArAd~ : see, again, murid~N .]) ― -b3- Also It (the sea) was, or became, tumultuous, with many waves. (M, L.)

sourceDefinition: quasi-pass. of 2; (S, L;) He, or it, was made, or caused, to return, go back, come back, or revert; &c.; or he, or it, returned, went back, came back, or reverted; much, frequently, again and again, or time after time. (L.) You say, tarad~adotu A_ilaY fulaAnK I returned time after time to such a one (Msb.) And huwa yatarad~adu A_ilaY majaAlisi AlEilomi He repairs frequently to, or frequents, the assemblies of science; syn. yaxotalifu . (A.) See also 6. ― -b2- [And as the returning repeatedly involves the going repeatedly, it signifies also, like Axtlf , He, or it, went, or moved, repeatedly, to and fro; so went and came; or reciprocated. Thus,] tarad~udu Al$~aYo'i AlmuEal~aqi fiY AlhawaA='i [means The moving to and fro of a thing suspended in the air ]. (K in art. *b .) You say, trd~dt Alr~uwHu The soul, or spirit, went and came. (W p. 5.) ― -b3- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) He wavered, or vacillated, fiY Alr~aA^oYi [ in opinion ]: (MA:) and fiY AlA^amori [ in the affair ], (S and K in art. lv , &c.,) and bayona A^amorayoni [ between two things, or affairs ]. (S and K in art. *b , &c.) And trd~d fiY SadoriY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) [ Such a thing became agitated to and fro in my mind, or bosom ]. (TA in art. rjE .) And trd~d said of a man, (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, confounded, or perplexed, so that he was unable to see his right course. (Bd and Jel in ix. 45.) [And (assumed tropical:) He laboured, or exerted himself, as though going to and fro, or making repeated efforts, in an affair: a meaning well known.] ― -b4- [And It was, or became, repeated time after time, or reiterated: it was, or became, reproduced: it was, or became, renewed. ] You say, trd~d Sawotuhu fiY Haloqihi His voice was, or became, reiterated in his throat, or fauces. (The Lexicons passim.) And trd~dfiY AlfaA='i [ He reiterated in uttering the letter f ; or, as the meaning is shown to be in the K in art. fA^ , he reiterated the letter f ( rad~ada AlfaA='a )]. (S in art. fA^ .) And trd~A_ fiY AljawaAbi wataEav~ara lisaAnuhu [ He reiterated, or stam- mered, or stuttered, in uttering the reply, and his tongue halted, faltered, or hesitated ]. (A.)

definition: Stones put, or joined, together, (S, M, O, Msb, K,) [ whether artificially or naturally, and particularly] in a channel of water: (O, K:) n.
sourceDefinition: Stones put, or joined, together, (S, M, O, Msb, K,) [ whether artificially or naturally, and particularly] in a channel of water: (O, K:) n. un. ↓ raSafapN . (S, M, O, Msb, K.) A dam constructed for [ the purpose of obstructing or retaining ] water: [such is now termed ↓ raSiyfN ; which is originally an epithet, but thus used as a subst., and commonly applied to a quay; and a bank, generally of masonry or bricks, raised along the side of a river or of a lake &c.; and any similar mass of masonry: ] also (i. e. raSafN ) the channel of a [ reservoir such as is termed ] maSonaEap . (M.) [Hence,] maA='u Alr~aSafi The water descending from the mountains, upon the rocks. (K.) El-'Ajjáj says, mino raSafK naAzaEa sayolFA raSafaA meaning that the wine of which he is speaking was mixed with water of a raSaf [or ledge of rocks or stones ] that had contended, in flowing, with another raSaf , because of its thereby becoming more clear and more delicate: he suppresses the word signifying water, meaning it to be understood, (saying mino raSafK for mino maA='i raSafK , [but in both of my copies of the S, maA='K is erroneously put for maA='i ,]) and he calls its passing ( masiyrahu [in the O and in one of my copies of the S masylahu ]) from rSf to rSf its contending therewith [i. e. with the latter rSf ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- See also raSafapN .

A dam constructed for [ the purpose of obstructing or retaining ] water: [such is now termed ↓ raSiyfN ; which is originally an epithet, but thus used as a subst., and commonly applied to a quay; and a bank, generally of masonry or bricks, raised along the side of a river or of a lake &c.; and any similar mass of masonry: ] also (i. e. raSafN ) the channel of a [ reservoir such as is termed ] maSonaEap . (M.) [Hence,] maA='u Alr~aSafi The water descending from the mountains, upon the rocks. (K.) El-'Ajjáj says, mino raSafK naAzaEa sayolFA raSafaA meaning that the wine of which he is speaking was mixed with water of a raSaf [or ledge of rocks or stones ] that had contended, in flowing, with another raSaf , because of its thereby becoming more clear and more delicate: he suppresses the word signifying water, meaning it to be understood, (saying mino raSafK for mino maA='i raSafK , [but in both of my copies of the S, maA='K is erroneously put for maA='i ,]) and he calls its passing ( masiyrahu [in the O and in one of my copies of the S masylahu ]) from rSf to rSf its contending therewith [i. e. with the latter rSf ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- See also raSafapN .

definition: A thing, (M,) an old and decayed bone, (A, TA,) or anything, (L, TA,) broken, broken in pieces, crushed, bruised, brayed, or pounded;
sourceDefinition: A thing, (M,) an old and decayed bone, (A, TA,) or anything, (L, TA,) broken, broken in pieces, crushed, bruised, brayed, or pounded; (M, L, TA;) or crumbled, or broken into small pieces with the hand; (A, TA;) or a thing that has become old and worn out, and crumbled, or broken into small pieces: ('Ináyeh, TA: [see marofuwtN :]) or broken, or crumbled, particles; fragments, or crumbs; of a thing that is dry, (T, S, A, K, TA,) of any kind; (T;) [as, for instance,] of musk. (A, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xvii. 52 and 100], A^ay^i*aA kun~aA EiZaAmFA warufaAtFA When we shall have become bones and broken particles? (S, M, TA.) [Hence also the phrase] laA birofaAtika , meaning No, by thy ancestors who have become broken and crumbled bones in the dust. (Har p. 634.) A_iroqaAqN ; (TA;) contr. of gal~aZahu ; (K;) or He made it, or rendered it, raqiyq [i. e. thin, as meaning of little thickness in comparison with its breadth and length together; &c.: see 1, first sentence; and raqiyqN , below]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] taroqiyqu AlkalaAmi (assumed tropical:) The making speech to be [ soft or tender, or easy and sweet, or] elegant, graceful, or ornate; the beautifying, or embellishing, and adorning, of speech. (S, TA.) And hence, (TA,) it is said in a prov., (S,) A^aEano SabuwHK turaq~iqu (S, K, TA) (tropical:) Dost thou allude (K, TA) gracefully, courteously, politely, or delicately, (TA,) to a morning-draught? (K, TA:) [the origin of which prov. was this:] a certain man named Jábán alighted by night at the abode of a people, and they entertained him, and gave him an evening-draught; and when he had finished it, he said, “ When ye shall have given me a morning draught, how shall I enter upon my way and prosecute the object of my want? ” whereupon the saying above was addressed to him: (K, * TA:) it is applied to him who makes an allusion to a thing, like this guest, who desired to oblige the people to give him the morning draught: and was said by Esh-Shaabee to one who spoke of kissing a woman when meaning thereby jimaAE . (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] rq~q Sawotahu (K in art. Hzn ) or ↓ Arqhu (S in that art.) (assumed tropical:) [ He made his voice slender, or soft, or gentle ]. ― -b4- taroqiyqN also signifies (assumed tropical:) [The pronouncing a word with the slender sound of the lengthened fet-h ( like the sound of “ a ” in our word “ father ”), and with the ordinary sound of the letter l ; both as in biAll~`hi and ll~`hi ;] the contr. of tafoxiymN . (Kull p. 127.) ― -b5- rq~q Alma$oYa , said of a camel, (K, TA,) (tropical:) He went an easy pace: and ↓ trq~q , alone, signifies the same. (TA.) [See also R. Q. 2.] ― -b6- rq~q bayona Alqawomi (assumed tropical:) He created, or excited, disorder, disturbance, disagreement, or dissension, or he made, or did, mischief, between, or among, the people. (TA.)

Hn :) in the soul, it is the contr. of jafowapN and qasowapN . sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) fem. with p , (TA,) Having the quality termed diq~apN ; (K, TA; [see 1, first sentence, respecting a mistranscription in the CK;]) as also ↓ ruqaAqN , (K,) of which the fem. is likewise with p ; (TA;) and ↓ ruq~aAqN , (K,) like rum~aAnN ; (TA;) [i. e.] contr. of galiyZN ; (S, Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ raq~N (K, TA) and ↓ riq~N : (K:) and contr. of vaxiynN : (S, TA:) [or rather this last is the proper explanation of raqiyqN , as well as of all the other epithets above mentioned; (see riq~apN ;) i. e. thin as meaning having little thickness in comparison with its breadth and length together; having little extent, or depth, between its two opposite surfaces: ] applied to bread that is [flat, flattened, or] expanded; such as is termed ruqaAqN , q. v.: (TA:) and to a garment, or piece of cloth, (Mgh, El-Munáwee, TA,) and the like, as meaning thin, fine, delicate, flimsy, unsubstantial, or uncompact, in texture &c.; contr. of SafiyqN ; (El-Munáwee, TA;) as also ↓ ruqaAriqN : (TA:) and to water [as meaning shallow, or of little depth; and in like manner to sand]: see ruq~N : (IDrd, K, TA:) [ thin as meaning wanting in spissitude; applied to mud &c.: attenuated: ] pl. riqaAqN (TA) and A^ariq~apN . (JK.) [Hence,] Alr~aqiyqaAni The part between the xaASirap [or flank ] and the rufog [or groin, on either side ]: (AA, K:) and the pl. AlA^arq~apu the thin parts at the flanks of she-camels. (JK.) Also, the dual, AlrqyqAn , The HiDonaAni [or part between the armpit and the flank, on either side ]. (K, TA. [In the CK AlxuSoyAni , q. v.]) And [ The two veins called ] the A^axodaEaAni [q. v.]. (K.) And, of the nose, The two sides: (K:) so says As: or the raqiyq of the nose is the thin and soft part of the side. (TA.) ― -b2- [Also Thin, or attenuated, and consequently (assumed tropical:) weak, in the bones: see raqaqN .] You say naAqapN raqiyqapN meaning (assumed tropical:) A she-camel whose marrow-bones have become weak and thin ( DaEufato waraq~ato ), and whose medullary canal is wide: pl. riqaAqN and raqaAy^iqu . (IAar, TA.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) Weak: and abject, mean, paltry, or contemptible: applied to a man [&c.]. (TA.) And goats are called maAlN raqiyqN [ Weak cattle ] because they have not the endurance of sheep. (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) Weak-hearted. (Mgh.) And raqiyqu Alqalobi (assumed tropical:) Soft, or tender, of heart; contr. of qaAsiY Alqalobi . (El-Munáwee, TA.) ― -b5- [(assumed tropical:) Soft or tender, or easy and sweet, or elegant, graceful, or ornate, speech or language.] raqiyqu All~afoZi means [(assumed tropical:) Soft or tender, &c., of expression; applied to a man: and also soft or tender or] easy and sweet expression. (Har p. 8.) ― -b6- [(assumed tropical:) Slender, or soft, or gentle, applied to the voice.] ― -b7- rajulN raqiyqu AlHawaA$iY (assumed tropical:) A man gentle, gracious, or courteous, to his associates. (TA in art. H$Y .) And Eayo$N raqiyqu AlHawaA$iY (tropical:) A soft or delicate, pleasant, or plentiful and easy, life. (TA.) ― -b8- [ Eayo$N raqiyqN may sometimes mean the same: but it commonly means (assumed tropical:) Scanty living or sustenance. ] ― -b9- And fulaAnN raqiyqu Ald~iyni waAlHaAli (tropical:) [ Such a one is weak in respect of religion, and narrow in the circumstances of, or evil in, his state or condition: see riq~apN ]. (TA.) -A2- Also A slave, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) male and female; (Msb;) [but] the latter is [also] called raqiyqapN : (Lh, JK, TA:) and slaves; for it is used as sing. and pl.; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) like rafiyqN and xaliyTN : (TA:) accord. to Abu-l-'Abbás, so called because they are abject and submissive to their owner: (TA:) the pl. of raqiyqN is A^ariq~aA='u , (Msb, TA,) erroneously said in the K to be riqaAqN ; (TA;) and that of raqiyqapN is raqaAy^iqu . (Lh, TA.) Using it as pl., you say, h`w^ulaA='i raqiyqiY [ These are my slaves ]. (Mgh.) And layosa fiY Alr~aqiyqi SadaqapN , i. e. [ There is no poorrate ] in the case of slaves used for service [as distinguished from those that are for sale]. (Msb.) [See also muraq~N .]

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. yaruwbu , (T, S, &c.,) inf. n. rawobN , (Lth, T, Msb,) or ruw^uwbN , (S,) or both, (T, M, Mgh, K,) said of milk, (T, S, M, &c.,) It was, or became, thick, or coagulated: (M, A, Msb, K:) or was churned, and deprived of its butter: (M, * A, K: *) or it was, or became, fit to be churned: (T:) or thick, (S,) or having a compact pellicle upon its surface, and thick, or resembling liver so that it quivered, (Lth, T,) and fit to be churned: (Lth, T, S:) or such as had become thick; (Fr, A'Obeyd, T, S, * Mgh;) until its butter was taken forth; (Fr, A'Obeyd, T, S; *) or before and after it had been deprived of its butter. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] raAba damuhu , (T, M, A, K,) aor. as above, (T,) inf. n. rawobN , (M,) (tropical:) [ His blood is about to be shed; ] his death, or destruction, is at hand: (M, K:) said of one who has exposed himself to that which will cause his blood to be shed; (T;) of one who has exposed himself to slaughter: (A:) like the phrase yafuwru damuhu ; (T;) or like yagoliY damuhu : his blood being likened to milk that has become thick, and fit to be churned. (A.) ― -b3- And raAba Alr~ajulu , (As, T, S, &c.,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. rawobN (S, M, K) and ruw^uwbN , (M, K,) (tropical:) The man was, or became, confused, or disturbed, (As, T, S, K,) in his affair, or case, (As, T,) or in his reason, or intellect, (S, K,) and his opinion: (As, T, S:) or confounded, or perplexed; unable to see his right course: (M, K:) and languid in spirit, by reason of satiety, or drowsiness, (M, A,) or intoxication; as also raAbato nafosuhu : (A:) or he arose (M, K, TA) from sleep (M, TA) disordered in body and mind: (M, K, TA:) or he was intoxicated with sleep: (M, K:) or he was lazy, sluggish, or slothful. (Aboo-Sa'eed, T.) ― -b4- And raAba , (Th, M, K,) inf. n. rawobN ; (TA;) and ↓ rw~b , (Th, M,) inf. n. tarowiybN ; (K;) (assumed tropical:) He (a man, Th, M) was, or became, fatigued, or jaded. (Th, M, K.) And maTiy~apu fulaAnK ↓ raw~abato (assumed tropical:) The riding-camel of such a one was, or became, fatigued, or jaded. (T.) ― -b5- And raAba (assumed tropical:) He, or it, was, or became, quiet, still, or motionless. (IAar, T.) ― -b6- It is said in a prov., of him who does wrong and does right, [or of him who does right and does wrong,] huwa ya$uwbu wa yaruwbu , meaning, accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed, (assumed tropical:) He defends his companion [at one time], and is lazy or sluggish or slothful [at another time]: or it means he defends without energy at one time, and at another time is lazy or sluggish or slothful, so that he defends not at all: or, as some say, he mixes water with the milk, and so spoils it, and he makes it good; from the saying of IAar that raAba signifies A^aSolaHa ; but if it have this meaning, it is originally raA^aba , with hemz. (T. [See more in art. $wb .]) -A2- Accord. to IAar, raAba also signifies He suspected. (T. [But in this sense it seems to belong to art. ryb .]) -A3- Also He lied. (K. [But in the T, this signification is assigned to $aAba , not to raAba ; app. in relation to the prov. above cited.])

definition: The ferment of milk, (T, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) consisting of a sour portion, (S, TA,) which is put into milk in order that it may become such as is termed raAy^ib ;
sourceDefinition: The ferment of milk, (T, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) consisting of a sour portion, (S, TA,) which is put into milk in order that it may become such as is termed raAy^ib ; (T, S, Mgh, Msb, TA;) and ↓ rawobapN signifies the same as ruwbapN in this sense, (Kr, M, A, K,) and in the other senses which follow: (M:) this is the primary signification: (TA:) or ferment of milk which contains its butter, and when its butter has been taken forth; as also ↓ raAy^ibN in both of these two senses; (T;) or in the latter state it is termed ↓ raAy^ibN : (TA:) or (so in the A and K, but in the M “ and, ”) remains of milk (M, A, K, in the second of which, as in the last, this applies also to ↓ rawobapN ,) that has become such as is termed raAy^ib : (M:) or remains of milk left in the [ skin or vessel called ] mirowab in order that fresh milk, when poured upon it, may quickly become raAy^ib : (T:) and milk containing its butter: and also milk from which its butter has been taken forth: (Aboo-' Amr ElMutarriz, MF, TA.) It is said in a prov., $ubo $awobFA laka ruwbatuhu [ Mix thou a mixture, app. of thick and fresh milk: thine shall be what will remain of it ]: (S:) or laka baEoDuhu [ thine shall be some of it ]: (so Meyd:) it is like the saying AuHolubo HalabFA laka $aToruhu [expl. in art. $Tr ]: (S, Meyd:) and is applied in inciting to aid him in whom one will find profit, or advantage. (Meyd.) ― -b2- I. q. durodiY~N [as meaning A ferment ] such as is put into [ the beverage called ] nabiy* [ to make it ferment ]. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) What has collected of the seminal fluid (T, S, M, A, K) of a horse, (S, A,) or of a stallion, (M, K,) after resting from covering; (T, S, M, K;) and ↓ rawobapN in this sense is mentioned by Lh: (M:) you say, A^aEironiY ruwabapa faHolika , (T,) or farasika , (S, A,) when you ask a person to lend you a stallion, or a horse, to cover: (T, S, A:) or the collecting thereof: or the seminal fluid of the stallion in the womb of the camel: (M, K:) it is thicker than that which is termed muhaAp , and more remote in respect of the place into which it is injected. (M.) ― -b4- (tropical:) Strength of a horse to run: so in the phrase farasN baAqiY Alr~uwbapi (tropical:) [ A horse whose strength to run remains ]. (A.) ― -b5- (tropical:) Intellect (IAar, S, A) of a man (IAar, S) when it has attained to full vigour: (A:) [app. as being likened to the rwbp of the stallion:] so in the saying, huwa yuHad~ivuniY wa A^anaA A_i*o *aAka gulaAmN layosa liY ruwbapN (tropical:) [ He would talk to me, I being then a boy, not having full intellect ]. (IAar, S, A: in one of my copies of the S, and in the TA, layosato .) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) The main, or most essential, part, syn. jum~aAE , of an affair: (M, K:) so in the saying, maA yaquwmu biruwbapi A^amorihi (assumed tropical:) [ He does not undertake, or superintend, or attend to, the main, or most essential, part of his affair ]: app. from the rwbp of the stallion. (M.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) Means of subsistence: (M, K:) (assumed tropical:) food, or sustenance: (TA:) (assumed tropical:) anything that puts a thing into a good, right, or proper state; from the same word as signifying “ a sour ferment that is put into milk to make it ferment: ” (JM:) (tropical:) a want, or thing that is needed [ to put one into a good, or right, state ]: (S, M, A, K:) and want as meaning poverty. (Ibn-Es-Seed, K, TA.) You say, laA yaquwmu biruwbapi A^aholihi , (S, A,) or maA yaquwmu Alx , (M, TA,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He will not, or does not, undertake, or take upon himself, or attend to, ] the food, or sustenance, of his family: or (assumed tropical:) their case, and the putting them into a good, right, or proper, state: (TA:) or (tropical:) [ the supplying of ] what they require of him. (S, M, A, TA.) ― -b8- (tropical:) A part, or portion, or small portion, ( TaAy^ifapN , S, M, or qiToEapN , K, or saAEapN , T, M, A,) of the night: (T, S, M, A, K:) [app. from the same word signifying “ remains of milk; ” as seems to be implied in the A:] so in the saying, maDato ruwbapN mina All~ayoli (tropical:) A period, or short portion, ( sAEp ,) of the night passed: (T, M, TA:) and baqiyato ruwbapN mina All~ayoli (tropical:) A period, or short portion, ( sAEp ,) of the night remained: (M, A, TA:) and hariqo Ean~aA mino ruwbapi All~ayoli , (S, A,) i. e. Aikosiro Ean~aA saAEapF minohu [app. for Aikosiro jahodanaA or the like, i. e. (tropical:) Abate thou, or allay thou, our fatigue, or the like, or relieve thou us, for a period, or short portion, of the night; mn before rwbp being redundant]. (A.) ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) A piece of flesh-meat: (M, K:) so in the saying, qaTaEa All~aHoma ruwbapF ruwbapF (assumed tropical:) [ He cut the flesh-meat into pieces; or cut it piece by piece ]. (M.) -A2- (assumed tropical:) Heaviness, sluggishness, or torpidness, (T, K,) or laxness, or confusedness of the intellect, (T,) and languor, feebleness, or faintness, (K,) from drinking much milk. (T.) -A3- Good and fertile land, abounding with plants, or herbage, (T, M, K,) and with trees: (T, M:) that kind of land in which the herbage, or pasturage, remains longest. (T.) ― -b2- Accord. to Aboo-' Amr Esh-Sheybánee, i. q. ma$aArapN , which means A saAqiyap [or channel of water for irrigation: but it has also other meanings, which see in art. $wr ]. (TA.) ― -b3- The tree called nulok ; (T, K, TA;) expl. by Ibn-Es-Seed as meaning the tree called zuEoruwr [q. v.]. (TA.) -A4- A kind of hooked instrument ( kal~uwb ) by means of which an animal that is hunted is drawn forth from its hole: (M, K:) accord. to Abu-l-'Omeythil, the miHora$ [app. meaning the same, or an instrument used for drawing forth the lizard called Dab~ from its hole ]. (M.) -A5- It is also mentioned by IAar as [syn. with rubapN and A^urobapN ,] meaning A knot. (T.) -A6- A piece of wood with which a wooden bowl, or other vessel, is repaired, or mended; or with which a breach, or broken place, therein is stopped up: (T, TA:) and, accord. to AZ, a patch, or piece, with which a camel's saddle ( raHol ) is patched, or pieced, when it is broken: (TA:) pl. ruwabN : but this is [properly, or originally, ruw^obapN ,] with ' : (T, TA:) so says ISk. (T.) [See art. rA^b .]

definition: , applied to milk, (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , applied to milk, (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) and ↓ rawobN , so applied, (Lth, T, M, K,) Thick, or coagulated: (M, Msb, K:) or churned, and deprived of its butter: (As, T, M, K:) see also ruwbapN , in two places: or thick, (S,) or having a compact pellicle upon its surface, and thick, or resembling liver so that it quivers, (Lth, T,) and fit to be churned: (Lth, T, S:) or such as has been churned, and such as has not been churned: (S:) or such as has become thick; (Fr, A 'Obeyd, T, S, Mgh;) until its butter is taken forth; (Fr, A 'Obeyd, T, S;) or before and after its butter has been taken forth; (Mgh;) like as the epithet Eu$araA='u is applied to a she-camel when pregnant and when she has brought forth. (A 'Obeyd, T, S.) A poet, cited by As, says, wa mano laka biAlr~aAy^ibi AlxaAviri saqaAka A^abuw maA EizK raAy^ibFA (T, S Mgh) meaning Aboo-Má'iz gave thee to drink churned [ milk ], (T, S,) but how wilt thou obtain, (T,) or [rather] but who will be answerable to thee for, (S,) the unchurned (T, S) [ that is thick, or] that has not had its butter taken forth from it? (S. [Or raAy^ib in the former instance may be from raAba of which the aor. is yariybu ; so that it may there mean what occasioned doubt, or evil opinion: see raAy^ibN in art. ryb : and if so, this word as belonging to the present art., and applied to milk, may signify only thick, or unchurned.]) And one says, maA Einodahu $awobN wa laA ↓ rawobN , (T,) or maA EinodiY Alx , (M,) i. e. He has not, or I have not, mixed honey, nor milk such as is termed raAy^ib : (T, M:) or, as some say, honey nor milk; thus explaining the two words $wb and rwb without restriction. (M. [See also art. $wb .]) ― -b2- [Hence,] raAy^ibN applied to a man, (T, S, M, A, K,) as also ↓ rawobaAnu , (T, M, K,) and ↓ A^arowabu , (M, K,) (tropical:) Confused, disturbed, or disordered, (T, S, A,) in mind, by reason of drowsiness, or satiety, or intoxication: (A:) or confounded, or perplexed; unable to see his right course: (M, K:) and languid in spirit, by reason of satiety, or drowsiness: (M:) or who has arisen (M, K) from sleep (M) disordered in body and mind: or intoxicated with sleep: (M, K:) or raAy^ibN signifies (assumed tropical:) confused in his intellect and his opinion and his affair: (TA:) and a man (tropical:) fatigued, wearied, distressed, embarrassed, or troubled: (A:) fem. [of the first] raAy^ibapN : (Lh, M:) pl. of the first, (S, M, A, * Mgh,) accord. to As, (S,) or of the second, rawobaY : (S, A, Mgh:) you say qawomN rawobaY (tropical:) a people, or company of men, confused, disturbed, or disordered, in minds, (T, S, Mgh,) by reason of drowsiness: (Mgh:) accord. to Sb, (M,) rendered heavy, or weak, or languid, by journeying, (S, M,) and by pain, (M,) and heavy with sleep: (S:) or intoxicated by drinking [ milk such as is termed ] raAy^ib . (S, Mgh.) ― -b3- And raAy^ibN also signifies (tropical:) A thing, or an affair, that is clear, or free from dubiousness or confusedness; (Th, T and TA in art. ryb ;) like the milk so termed. (TA in art. ryb . See an ex. in that art.)

definition: The eleventh letter of the alphabet;
sourceDefinition: The eleventh letter of the alphabet; commonly called zaAYN , and sometimes zaA='N , [and zFA , and zaA , (see zaAYN in art. zwY ,)] and zaY~N , and zaYo . (MF.) It is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; and of the letters termed A^asilay~ap , because proceeding from the tip of the tongue. (TA.) Az says that it is not conjoined with S in any Arabic word. (TA.) It is substituted for s and for S ; as in yazodilu for yasodilu , and yazoduqu for yaSoduqu : and in the Tes-heel it is said that it is sometimes interchanged [with s ] after j , as in jusotu xilaAla Ald~iyaAri for juzotu ; and after r , as in rasaba and razaba : which interchange, accord. to MF, is said to be of the dial. of Kelb; or, as Et-Toosee says, of the dial. of 'Odhrah and Kaab and Benul-' Ambar. (TA.) -A2- [As a numeral, z denotes Seven. ]

sourceDefinition: , aor. yazokuw , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. zakaA='N , (S,) or zukuw~N , (Msb, [accord. to which the former seems to be a simple subst.,]) or both, (K, TA,) the latter like Euluw~N , as in the M, but accord. to [some of] the copies of the K zakowN , (TA,) It increased, or augmented; (S, Msb, K, TA;) it received increase and blessing from God; it throve by the blessing of God; (Er-Rághib, TA;) and produced fruit; (TA in art. zkY ;) and zakiYa , (K in that art.,) aor. yazokaY , inf. n. zakaApN , (TA in that art.,) signifies the same, (K, TA,) mentioned by ISd, on the authority of Lh, as a dial. var. of zakaA , aor. yzkw ; (TA;) and so ↓ AzkY ; (Msb, K;) and ↓ tzk~Y : (K in art. zkY :) it is said of seed-produce, (S, Msb, Er-Rághib, TA,) and of wealth, or cattle &c., and of other things: of anything that increases, or augments, one says yazokuw , inf. n. zakaA='N . (TA.) [This is the primary meaning: or, accord. to some, the primary meaning is, It was, or became, pure: ] some say that the root denotes purity: and some, that it denotes a state of increase, or augmentation. (Mgh.) You say also zakati AlA^aroDu The land throve, or yielded increase. (Msb.) And zakaA AlgulaAmu [ The boy grew, or throve ], inf. n. zukuw~N and zakaA='N , on the authority of Akh. (S.) And zakaA Eamaluhu (assumed tropical:) [ His deed, or work, throve ]. (K in art. dr .) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, AlmaAlu tanoquSuhu Aln~afaqapu waAlEilomu yazokuw EalaY AlA_inofaAqi (assumed tropical:) [ Wealth, what one expends diminishes it, but knowledge increases by expending ]: zakaA=' being thus predicated of knowledge, though this is not a corporeal thing. (TA.) Accord. to El-Umawee, (S,) said of a man, zakaA , (S, K,) aor. yazokuw , inf. n. zukuw~N , (S,) means He enjoyed, or led, a plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, life; (S, K;) was in a state of abundance of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life. (S.) And likewise said of a man, (having the same aor. and inf. n., TA,) it means also He was, or became, good, or righteous; (Jel in xxiv. 21, Msb, K, TA;) and pure from sin. (Jel ibid.) [Hence,] h`*aA AlA^amoru laA yazokuw bifulaAnK means This thing, or affair, will not be suitable to such a one; will not befit him. (S.)

definition: A pair, or couple;
sourceDefinition: A pair, or couple; two coupled together; (S, K, TA;) [of men, and] of ships and other things; (TA;) i. q. zawojN : (K, and T in art. tw :) opposed to taw~N meaning “ one, and no more. ” (K, and TA in this art. and in art. tw .) You say, jaA='a fulaAnN zaw~FA , meaning Such one came with his companion. (S.) [See also art. tw .] -A2- Alz~aw~u is also the name of A ship constructed by ElMutawekkil, (K, TA,) the 'Abbásee; in which he associated in drinking with the poet El-Boh- turee. (TA.) Accord. to the S, it is the name of a mountain in El-'Irák: but Aboo-Zekereeyà EtTebreezee, and after him the author of the K, deny this, and suppose J to have been led into error in asserting such to be the case by the following saying of the poet above mentioned: walaA jabalFA kaAlz~aw~i yuwqafu taArapF wayanoqaAdu A_im~aA qudotahu bizimaAmi [ Nor have I seen a mountain like Alz~aw~ , that is made stationary at one time, and becomes led on at another time if thou draw it along with a leading-rope ]: J, however, does not say that he took this from the poetry of El-Bohturee. (TA. [In the CK, in the verse above cited, Ai*o mA is put in the place of A_im~aA .]) -A3- [J also says that,] accord. to As, zaw~u Almaniy~api signifies What happens of decreed perdition or death: and zaw~N is also said to signify a decree [of God]: (S, TA:) and in the M it is said that zaw~N signifies perdition, or death: and zaw~u Almaniy~api , the accidents, or calamities, of destiny or death: but accord. to the T, As said zawo'u Almaniy~api , with ' (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (K,) aor. yazowiyhi , (TA,) inf. n. zaY~N and zuwiY~N , (K, TA,) the latter [accord. to the CK zawoYN , but it is correctly] like EutiY~N , (TA,) He put it aside, or away, or apart; or removed it from its place. (K.) You say, zawaYa Eanohu ka*aA , inf. n. zuwiY~N , He averted, diverted, or removed, from him such a thing; turned, put, or sent, it away, or back, from him. (TA.) ― -b2- And zawaY sir~ahu Eanohu He concealed his secret from him. (K.) ― -b3- Also (K) zawaAhu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, inf. n. zaY~N , (Msb, TA,) He drew it, collected it, or gathered it, together; contracted it, or grasped it. (S, Msb, K.) definition: He was, or became, [or placed himself, ] in a zaAwiyap , i.
sourceDefinition: He was, or became, [or placed himself, ] in a zaAwiyap , i. e. corner, of a house or chamber; as also ↓ zw~Y , (K,) inf. n. tazowiyapN ; (TA;) and ↓ AnzwY . (K.) -A2- tazay~aA , from Alz~iY~u ; (K, KL;) or tazay~aA biziY~K ; (Lth, MA;) He invested himself with a garb, guise, or dress; [or with an external appearance; ] (MA, KL;) he decked, or adorned, himself. (MA.) You say of a man, tzy~A biziY~K HasanK [ He invested himself with a beautiful, or goodly, garb, &c.]. (Lth, TA.) Hence the saying of El-Mutanebbee, waqado yatazay~aA biAlhawaY gayoru A^aholihi wayasotaSoHibu AlA_inosaAnu mano laA yulaAy^imuho (TA:) i. e. [ And verily, or sometimes, or often, one who is not entitled to it ] assumes the guise of love; and the man asks to be his companion him who is not suited to him: (W p. 374:) his disciple Ibn-Jinnee, however, objected to him his saying ytzy~A , and expressed his opinion that the correct word is yatazaw~aY ; and El-Mutanebbee admitted that he did not know the former word in any [classical] poetry, nor in any lexicological book, but asserted the verb in use to be only tazay~aA : (MF, TA:) in the M it is said that IJ held tazay~aA to be originally tazawoyaA , and the w to be changed into Y because quiescent, and incorporated into the Y preceded by it. (TA.)

definition: A corner, or an angle, ( rukon ,) of a house or room or the like: (K:) of the measure faAEilapN from zawaY signifying jamaEa ;
sourceDefinition: A corner, or an angle, ( rukon ,) of a house or room or the like: (K:) of the measure faAEilapN from zawaY signifying jamaEa ; because of its em- bracing ( liA^an~ahaA jamaEato ) a part, or portion, ( quTorFA ,) thereof: (Msb, TA:) pl. zawaAyaA [which is irreg.; for by rule it should be zawaA='K , being originally of the measure fawaAEilu , not faEaAy^ilu ]. (S, K.) They say, kamo fiY Alz~awaAyaA mina AlxabaAyaA [ How many hidden things are there in the corners! ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [In geometry, An angle. ― -b3- And hence, zaAwiyapu AlEaw~aA='i The star γ of Virgo; AlEaw~aA='u being composed of four stars, γ,δ,ε and η of Virgo, disposed nearly in the form of a capital L, with ε, δ, γ from top to bottom and η to the right. ] ― -b4- In a saying cited voce raAwiyapN , the pl. zawaAyaA is used as meaning Houses, or tents. (T in art. rwY .) ― -b5- [And in the present day, the term zaAwiyapN is also applied to A small mosque, or chapel: and in some instances, a building of this kind, thus called, serves as a hospice, or an asylum for poor Muslims, students and others; like ribaATN .]

definition: , aor. , inf. n. saboHN (Msb, K) and sibaAHapN , (S, * K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He swam, syn. EaAma , (S, * K,) biAln~ahori and fiyhi [ in the river ], (K,) or rather biAlmaA='i...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. saboHN (Msb, K) and sibaAHapN , (S, * K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He swam, syn. EaAma , (S, * K,) biAln~ahori and fiyhi [ in the river ], (K,) or rather biAlmaA='i (MF, TA) or fY AlmaA='i (Msb) [i. e. in the water ], for it is likewise in the sea, and in a pool, and also in any expanse: (MF, TA:) [or he swam upon the surface, without immersing himself; for,] accord. to Z, there is a difference between EawomN and sibaAHapN ; the former signifying the “ coursing along in water with immersion of oneself; ” and the latter, the coursing along upon water without immersion of oneself. (MF, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Aln~ujuwmu tasobaHu fiY Alfalaki (A, TA) (tropical:) The stars [ swim, or glide along, or] pass along, in the firmament, with a spreading forth. (TA.) It is said in the Kur xxi. 34 and xxxvi. 40, with reference to the sun and the moon, (Bd and Jel in xxi. 34,) with which the stars are meant to be included, (Jel ibid.,) kul~N fiY falakK yasobaHuwna , i. e. (assumed tropical:) All [ glide or] travel along swiftly, [ in a firmament, ] like the swimmer (Bd and Jel ibid.) upon the surface of the water, (Bd ibid.,) or in the water; (Jel ibid.;) wherefore the form of the verb used is that which is appropriate to rational beings, (Bd and Jel ibid.,) swimming being the act of such beings. (Bd ibid.) ― -b3- And [hence] one says, sabaHa *ikoruka Al$~amosi wa Alqamari ↓ masaAbiHa (tropical:) [ Thy fame has travelled as far as the sun and the moon; lit., swum along the tracts along which swim the sun and the moon ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- [Hence, likewise, as inf. n. of sabaHa , aor. as above,] saboHN also signifies (tropical:) The running of a horse (S, L, K, * TA) in which the fore legs are stretched forth well [ like as are the arms of a man in swimming ]. (L, K, * TA.) ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) The being quick, or swift. (MF.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) The being, or becoming, remote. (MF.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) The travelling far. (K.) You say, sabaHa fiY AlA^aroDi (assumed tropical:) He went, or travelled, far, in, or into, the land, or country: (O, TA:) and sabaxa : both thus expl. by Abu-l-Jahm El-Jaafaree. (TA.) ― -b8- And (assumed tropical:) The journeying for the purpose of traffic ( taqal~ub [q. v.]); and [a people's] becoming scattered, or dispersed, in the land, or earth. (K.) And (assumed tropical:) The busying oneself in going to and fro, or seeking gain, (IAar, TA,) and occupying oneself according to his own judgment or discretion, in the disposal or management of affairs, in respect of the means of subsistence. (IAar, S, K, TA.) You say, fulaAnN yasobaHu Aln~ahaAra kul~ahu fiY Talabi AlmaEaA$i (tropical:) [ Such a one busies himself in going to and fro, or occupies himself according to his own judgment or discretion, in seeking the means of subsistence ]. (A, TA.) And sabaHa fiY HawaAy^ijihi (assumed tropical:) He occupied himself according to his own judgment or discretion in the accomplishment of his needful affairs. (Msb.) ― -b9- As used in the Kur [lxxiii. 7], where it is said, A_in~a laka fiY Aln~ahaAri saboHFA TawiylFA , it is variously explained: (S, TA:) accord. to Katádeh (S) and El-Muärrij, (S, TA,) the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) [ Verily thou hast in the day-time ] long freedom from occupation; (S, K, * TA;) and in this sense, also, its verb is sabaHa , aor. : (JM:) [thus it has two contr. significations:] or, accord. to Lth, (assumed tropical:) leisure for sleep: (TA:) accord. to AO, the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) long-continued scope, or room, for free action; syn. mutaqal~abFA TawiylFA : and accord. to ElMuärrij, it means also (assumed tropical:) coming and going: (S, TA:) accord. to Fr, the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) thou hast in the day-time the accomplishment of thy needful affairs: (TA:) or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) [ long ] occupation of thyself in thy affairs of business; not being free from occupation therein for the reciting of the Kur-án. (Jel.) Some read saboxFA , which has nearly the same meaning as saboHFA . (Zj, TA.) ― -b10- As inf. n. of sabaHa , (TK,) it signifies also (assumed tropical:) The state of sleeping. (K.) And as such also, (TK,) (assumed tropical:) The being still, quiet, or motionless. (K.) ― -b11- [Also (assumed tropical:) The glistening of the mirage.] You say, sabaHa Als~araAbu , or AlA=lu , meaning lamaEa [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The mirage glistened ]. (O.) ― -b12- And (assumed tropical:) The digging, or burrowing, in the earth, or ground. (K, * TA.) You say of the jerboa, sabaHa fiY AlA^aroDi (assumed tropical:) He dug, or burrowed, in the earth, or ground. (O, TA.) ― -b13- And (assumed tropical:) The being profuse in speech. (K.) You say, sabaHa fiY AlkalaAmi (assumed tropical:) He was profuse in speech. (O, TA.) ― -b14- See also the next paragraph. in two places.

definition: signifies The declaring [God] to be far removed, or free, from every imperfection or impurity, or from everything derogatory from [his] glory;
sourceDefinition: signifies The declaring [God] to be far removed, or free, from every imperfection or impurity, or from everything derogatory from [his] glory; syn. tanoziyhN , (S, O, Msb, TA,) and taqodiysN : (Msb:) the magnifying, celebrating, lauding, or praising, and glorifying, God; and declaring Him to be far removed, or free, from everything evil. (TA.) You say, sab~aHa A@ll~`ha , (T, A, Mgh, Msb, TA,) and sb~H lil~`hi , (Kur lvii. 1 &c., and A,) in which the l is redundant, (Jel in lvii. 1 &c.,) inf. n. tasobiyHN , and suboHaAnN is a subst. that [sometimes] stands in the place of the inf. n., (T, TA,) or it is an inf. n. of which the verb is sabaHa , (K, TA,) He declared God to be far removed, or free, from every imperfection or impurity &c., (A, Mgh, TA,) or from what they say [ of Him ] who disacknowledge [ his attributes ]; (Msb;) [i. e. he declared, or celebrated, or extolled, the perfection or purity, or absolute glory, of God; ] and he magnified, celebrated, lauded, or praised, God, by the mention of his names, saying suboHaAna A@ll~`hi and the like: (Msb:) and sb~H [alone], (Mgh, K,) inf. n. tasobiyHN , (K,) he said suboHaAna A@ll~`hi ; (Mgh, K;) as also ↓ sabaHa , inf. n. suboHaAnN ; (K, TA;) the latter, which is like $akara , inf. n. $ukoraAnN , a dial. var. mentioned by ISd; and no regard should be paid to the saying of Ibn-Ya'eesh and others, that sbHAn is an inf. n. of which the verb is obsolete: accord to El-Mufaddal, suboHaAnN is the inf. n. of ↓ sabaHa signifying he raised his voice with supplication, or prayer, and magnification or celebration or praise [ of God, as when one says suboHaAna A@ll~`hi or the like ]; and he cites as an ex., qabaHa A@loA_il`hu wajuwha tagoliba kul~amaA sabaHa AlHajiyju wa kab~aruwA A_iholaAlaA [ May God remove far from good, or prosperity, or success, the persons ( wujuwha here meaning nufuwsa ) of the tribe of Teghlib, whenever the pilgrims raise their voices with supplication, &c., and say Aall~`hu A^akobaro , ejaculating lab~ayoka ]. (MF, TA.) wanaHonu nusab~iHu biHamodika , in the Kur ii. 28, is a phrase denotative of state, (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) meaning While we declare thy remoteness from evil [ of every kind ], (Ksh, Bd,) or while we say suboHaAna A@ll~`hi , (Jel,) praising Thee, (Ksh,) [or with the praising of Thee, i. e.] making the praising of Thee to be an accompaniment, or adjunct, to our doing that: (Ksh, Bd, Jel:) so that we are the more worthy to be appointed thy vice-agents. (Ksh, * Bd, * Jel.) fasab~iHo biA@somi rab~ika AlEaZiymi , in the Kur lvi. 73 and last verse, means Therefore declare thou the remoteness from what is unsuitable to his majesty by mentioning the name of thy Lord, or by mentioning the Lord, for the pronouncing of the name of a thing is the mentioning of it, [i. e., of the thing itself,] the great name, or the great Lord: (Bd:) or it means therefore pray thou commencing with, or uttering, the name of thy Lord [ the great name or Lord]: (Kull p. 211:) [for] ― -b2- tasobiyHN also signfies The act of praying. (K, Msb.) You say, sab~aHa meaning He prayed. (A, Mgh.) And [particularly] He performed the [ supererogatory ] prayer of [ the period termed ] AlD~uHaY . (TA.) And fulaAnN yusab~iHu A@ll~`ha , i. e. ↓ yuSal~iY Als~aboHapa , meaning Such a one performs prayer to God, either obligatory or supererogatory: [but generally the latter: (see suboHapN :)] and yusab~iHu EalaY raAHilatihi performs supererogatory prayer [ upon his camel that he is riding ]. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [iii. 36], wasab~iHo biA@loEa$iY~i waA@loA_ibokaAra , i. e. And pray thou [ in the evening, or the afternoon, and the early morning ]. (TA.) And it is related of 'Omar, A^an~ahu jalada rajulayoni sab~aHaA baEoda AlEaSori , meaning [ That he flogged two men ] who prayed [ after the prescribed time of the afternoon-prayer ]. (S, TA.) You say also, biyadihi yusab~iHu bihaA ↓ suboHapN [i. e. In his hand is a string of beads by the help of which he repeats the praises of God: see suboHapN , below]. (A, Msb. *) ― -b3- Also The making an exception, by saying A_ino $aA='a A@ll~`hu [ If God will ]: because, by so saying, one magnifies God, and acknowledges that one should not will unless God will: and thus is expl. the saying in the Kur [lxviii. 28], A^alamo A^aqulo lakumo lawo laA tusab~iHuwna [ Did I not say to you, Wherefore will ye not make an exception? addressed to the owners of a garden, who “ swore that they would certainly cut its fruit when they should be entering upon the time of morning, they not making an exception ”]. (TA.)

definition: Garments of skins: (K:) or, accord.
sourceDefinition: Garments of skins: (K:) or, accord. to Sh, sibaAHN , which is the pl., signifies shirts of skins, for boys: AO corrupted the word, relating it as written subojapN , with j , and with damm to the s ; whereas this signifies “ a black [garment of the kind called] kisaA=' : ” and a verse cited by him as presenting an ex. of its pl., in its last word, is from a poem of which each verse has for its fundamental rhyme-letter the unpointed H : ISd, in art. sbj , mentions sibaAjN as signifying “ garments of skin, ” and having sbjp for its sing.; but says that the word with the unpointed H is of higher authority; though he also states it, in the same art., to have been corrupted by AO. (TA.) ― -b2- [A meaning belonging to suboHapN (q. v.) is assigned in some copies of the K to saboHapN .] -A2- Als~aboHapu , (K,) or saboHapu , from saAbiHN as an epithet applied to a horse, or mare, (IAth, TA,) is a proper name of A horse, or mare, belonging to the Prophet: (IAth, K, TA:) and of another belonging to Jaafar the son of Aboo- Tálib; (K;) or this was a mare named samoHapu : (O:) and of another belonging to another. (K.)

definition: Beads (S, Msb, K, TA) strung (Msb, TA) upon a string or thread, (TA,) [ ninety-nine in number, and having a mark after each thirtythree, ] with which ( by counting them, K) one performs the act...
sourceDefinition: Beads (S, Msb, K, TA) strung (Msb, TA) upon a string or thread, (TA,) [ ninety-nine in number, and having a mark after each thirtythree, ] with which ( by counting them, K) one performs the act termed Alt~asobiyH [meaning the repetition of the praises of God, generally consisting in repeating the words suboHaAna A@ll~`ho thirtythree times, AlHamodu lil~`ho thirty-three times, and Aall~`hu A^akobaro thirty-three times, which is done by many persons after the ordinary prayers, as a supererogatory act]: (S, A, Msb, K:) its appellation implies that it is an Arabic word; but Az says that it is post-classical: its pl. is subaHN (Msb) and subuHaAtN also. (Har p. 133.) See 2, last sentence but one. ― -b2- Also Invocation of God; or supplication: (K:) and prayer, (A, Msb,) whether obligatory or supererogatory: (Msb:) or supererogatory praise; (S;) and supererogatory prayer; (S, A, Mgh, K;) because of the tasobiyHN therein. (Mgh.) You say, fulaAnN yuSal~iY Als~uboHapa , expl. above; see 2, in the latter part of the paragraph. (Msb.) And qaDaYsuboHatahu He performed, or finished, his prayer: (A:) or qaDayotu suboHatiY means I performed, or finished, my supererogatory praise and such prayer. (S.) And Sal~aY Als~uboHapa He performed the supererogatory prayer: (A:) and suboHapa AlD~uHaY [ the supererogatory prayer of the period termed AlD~uHaY ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- suboHapu A@ll~`hi , (IAth, K, TA,) with damm, (TA, [but in my MS. copy of the K written saboHap , and so in the CK,]) means (assumed tropical:) The greatness, or majesty, of God: (IAth, K, TA:) or [the pl.] Als~ubuHaAtu , occurring in a trad., means (assumed tropical:) the greatness, or majesty, and the light [or splendour ], of God: (Msb:) or by the saying subuHaAtu wajohi rab~inaA , with damm to the s and b , is meant (assumed tropical:) the greatness, or majesty, of the face of our Lord: (S:) or subuHaAtu wajohi A@ll~`hi means (assumed tropical:) the lights [or splendours ], (K,) or, accord. to ISh, the light [or splendour ], (TA,) of the face of God: (ISh, K, TA:) some say that subuHaAtu Alwajohi means (assumed tropical:) the beauties of the face; because, when you see a person of beautiful face, you say, suboHaAna A@ll~`hi [to express your admiration]: and some, that [when it relates to God] it denotes a declaration of his being far removed from every imperfection; meaning suboHaAna wajohihi . (TA. [See suboHaAn .]) One says, [addressing God,] A^asoA^aluka bisubuHaAti wajohika Alkariymi , with two dammehs, meaning (tropical:) [ I ask Thee ] by the evidences of thy greatness, or majesty, [or of the greatness, or majesty, of thy glorious face, ] by the acknowledgement whereof thy praise is celebrated. (A.) ― -b4- Als~ubuHaAtu also signifies (assumed tropical:) The places of prostration [probably meaning in the reciting of the Kur-án ]. (K.) -A2- Also, i. e. [the sing.,] suboHapN , A piece of cotton. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: is the inf. n. of sabaHa as syn. with sab~aHa [q. v.]; (K, TA;) and is a subst. that [sometimes] stands in the place of the inf. n. of the latter of these verbs, i. e. in the sense of tasobiyHN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] saHaqati Alr~iyHu AlA^aroDa , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The wind effaced the traces of the ground, (K, TA,) and carried away the broken particles [ that were upon it ]: (M, TA:) or passed along as though it were bruising, or braying, or pounding, ( kaA^an~ahaA tasoHaqu ,) the dust: (O, K:) or pared, or abraded, the surface of the earth by its vehement blowing; as also sahakatohaA [q. v.]. (T, A, TA.) ― -b3- And saHaqahu , (K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He wore it out; namely, a garment. (K, TA.) And saHaqahu AlbilaA (assumed tropical:) [ Wear wasted it ]; namely, a garment. (TA.) ― -b4- Also He, or it, rendered it soft, or smooth; namely, a hard thing.
