sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taTah~urN , is sometimes changed into AiT~ah~ara , inf. n. AiT~ah~urN , the t being incorporated into the T , and this requiring a conjunctive A , (Sgh, K,) in order that the word may not begin with a quiescent letter: (Sgh:) and TahuwrN is also an inf. n. [or rather a quasi-inf. n.] (Sb, K) of taTah~ara , (Mgh, TA,) like as waDuwo'N is [said to be] of tawaD~aA^a . (TA.) The meaning is, [ He became cleansed, or purified: or he cleansed, or purified, himself: and] he washed himself. (Mgh.) You say, tTh~r biAlmaA='i [ He cleansed, or purified, or washed, himself with water ]: (S:) he performed the ablution termed AlwuDuwo' : and that termed AlAisotinojaA=' ; (A;) as also tTh~r alone, as used in the Kur ix. 109: (Mgh, TA:) and the same verb, alone, is expl. as signifying he made use of water, or what supplied its place; thus used in the Kur v. 9. (TA.) In the Kur vii. 80 and xxvii. 57, the verb is used derisively. (TA.) You say also, tTh~rt , (Mgh, Msb, K,) and AiT~ah~arato , (Mgh,) meaning, She cleansed, or purified, herself by washing, from [ the pollution of ] the menstrual discharge, (Mgh, Msb, K,) &c. ; (K;) as also ↓ Taharato and Tahurato ; (Msb, * K;) agreeably with what is said in the B, that Tahara and Tahura and AT~h~r and tTh~r have the same signification: (TA:) or tTh~rt and AT~h~rt have this signification; but the unaugmented verb has the signification first assigned to it, or “ her discharge of blood stopped: ” (Abu-l-'Abbás, IAar:) in the Kur ii. 222, some read Hat~aY yaTohurona ; and others, Hat~aY yaT~ah~arona : but the latter reading is the preferable, on account of the difference between the two forms of the verb, just mentioned: (Abu-l-'Abbás:) or the law which allows not the touching a woman until she has performed the ablution mentioned above shows the two forms of the verb to be the same in signification. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) He removed himself far from unclean things, or impurities. (S, Mgh, K. *) ― -b3- (tropical:) He refrained from sin, (K, TA,) and from what was not good: (TA:) he removed himself far from low, or ignoble, habits: and in this sense, accord. to some, it is used in the Kur vii. 80 and xxvii. 57. (TA.) And tTh~r mina AlA_ivomi (tropical:) He removed himself far from sin. (A.)

(Msb.)

ZaEaAy^inu and ZuEunN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and ZuEonN (S, K) and [pl. of pauc.] A^aZoEaAnN (S, Mgh, K) and pl. pl. ZuEunaAtN . (TA. [But see, in what follows, an assertion of AZ respecting the pl. ZuEunN .]) ― -b2- And A woman, (ISk, Mgh, Msb, TA;) whether in a hawodaj or elsewhere; (ISk, TA;) the word being used in the sense of maZoEuwnapN [for maZoEuwnN bihaA ]; because her husband journeys ( yaZoEanu ) with her: (Msb:) or a man's wife; because she journeys with her husband: (TA:) or a woman as long as she is in the hwdj ; (S, Msb, K;) when not in it she is not thus called: (S:) or this is the primary meaning: then it was applied to her though in her tent, because she might become maZoEuwnap [i. e. maZoEuwn bihaA ]: (Msb:) it is mostly applied to a woman riding [ in a hwdj ]: then, to a hwdj without a woman: and to a woman without a hwdj . (TA.) 'Amr Ibn-Kulthoom says, qifiY qabola Alt~afar~uqi yaA ZaEiynaA nuxab~iroki Alyaqiyna watuxobiriynaA [ Pause thou before separation, O woman in the camel-vehicle: we will inform thee of the real truth respecting our case, and thou shalt inform us respecting thy case]: (S:) yaA ZaEiynaA is for yaA ZaEiynapu . (EM p. 185.) ― -b3- And, accord. to Lth, A camel that is ridden by women: [like ZaEuwnN :] and applied to signify a woman because she rides it: or, accord. to IAmb, a camel upon which one journeys: and hence the trad., layosa fiY jamalK ZaEiynapK SadaqapN i. e. sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. EajorN , He bent his neck, (ISk, S, O, K, TA,) and twisted it: said of one who desires not to comply with a command to do a thing: or Eajara Eunuqahu A_ilaY ka*aA waka*aA [ he bent, and twisted, his neck, turning towards such and such things, ] is said of one who is going in a particular direction, and returns from it to a thing behind him which he is forbidden: so in the Nawádir el-Aaráb. (TA.) ― -b2- And one says, Eajara bihi baEiyruhu as though meaning His camel returned with him towards his usual associates and his family when he was desiring to ride him in a particular direction; as also Eakara bihi . (ISk, S, O.) [See also the latter verb.] ― -b3- And Eajara Alfarasu , (S, O,) aor. , inf. n. EajorN and EajaraAnN , (O,) The horse extended [or, accord. to an explanation of the act. part. n. in the L, raised ] his tail towards his Eajuz [or. croup ] in running. (S, O.) ― -b4- And hence, (S,) mar~a Alfarasu yaEojiru (S, O, K *) and yaEojuru , (so in one of my copies of the S, and accord. to the TA,) inf. n. EajorN (S, K) and EajaraAnN , (K,) The horse went along swiftly, (S, O, K, *) by reason of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, (O,) or from fear and the like: and ↓ muEaAjarapN is syn. with the inf. ns. of yaEojiru used in this sense: (K:) [so that one says in like manner ↓ mar~a yuEaAjiru :] and one says also, Alr~ajulu Alr~ajula ↓ EAjr , meaning The man ran before the man, fleeing. (O, TA.) ― -b5- Eajara , aor. , inf. n. EajorN , said of an ass, is syn. with qamaSa [app. as meaning He raised his fore legs together and put them down together, and beat the ground with his kind legs ]: (K, TA:) and a similar action is signified by the phrase yaEojiru birijolayohi , inf. n. EajaraAnN , [app. meaning He beats the ground with his kind legs, rearing while doing so ], said of a horse. (TA.) -A2- Eajarahu biAlEajoraA='i He beat him, or struck him, with the knotted staff or stick, so that the place struck became swollen; as also bajarahu . (O.) ― -b2- And Eajarotu Al$~aYo'a I clave, or split, the thing. (IKtt, TA.) ― -b3- And Eajara Ealayohi biAls~ayofi , (S, O, K, *) aor. , inf. n. EajorN , (K,) He made an assault, or attack, upon him with the sword. (S, O, K. *) ― -b4- Eajarotu Ealayohi , (Sh, O, K, *) aor. , inf. n. EajorN , (K,) is also syn. with Hajarotu Ealayohi [meaning I prohibited him from using, or disposing of, his property according to his own free will ]. (Sh, O, K. *) ― -b5- And EajorN is also syn. with A_iloHaAHN ; in which sense, as in others, its aor. is said in the K to be yaEojiru ; but this is not the case, for the verb is used only in the pass. form: you say, Eujira EalaY Alr~ajuli , meaning The man was importuned for his property, or was asked for it by many persons, so that it became little. (TA.) One says rajulN Ealayohi ↓ maEojuwrN meaning A man importuned by begging so that all his property has been taken from him. (K, * TA.) -A3- One says also, Eajara Alr~ajulu bivawobihi EalaY raA^osihi [app. meaning The man wound his garment upon his head: see 8]. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, Eajara Alr~iyqu EalaY A^anoyaAbihi (tropical:) The saliva became dry upon his canine teeth, and stuck. (TA.) -A4- Eajira , (S, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. EajarN , (S,) He (a man, S) was, or became, thick and fat. (S, O, K.) And Eajira , (K,) inf. n. EajarN , (S, O,) He (a man, S, O) was, or became, bigbellied. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- Also He (a horse) was, or became, hard (K, TA) in his flesh. (TA.) And Eajira , inf. n. EajarN and EujorapN , It (a solid hoof, and the belly,) was, or became, hard. (IKtt, TA.) [See also EajarN below.]

sourceDefinition: She (a woman) bound a miEojar [q. v.] upon her head; (S;) she attired herself with the miEojar : (O, Msb:) or with a ximaAr : (Mgh:) AiEotijaArN is a mode of attiring peculiar to a woman, (K, TA,) resembling that termed AilotiHaAfN . (TA.) ― -b2- And AEtjr He wound a turban round his head: (IF, S, Mgh, O, Msb:) and he wound a turban (or a piece of cloth, TA) upon his head without turning [ a portion of ] it beneath his lower jaw; (Az, El-Ghooree, Mgh, K, * TA;) as also AiqotaEaTa : the winding it in which manner [and so wearing it] in prayer, is forbidden: but another explanation, which is, he wound the turban upon his head so as to show the haAmap [or crown of the head ], is more probable; as it is from miEojarN , meaning “ a piece of a cloth, like a fillet, wound upon the round of a woman's head. ” (Mgh.) One says, ↓ huwa Hasanu AlmuEotajari He is comely in respect of the manner of winding the turban upon the head. (A.) [See also EijorapN : and see muEotajirN .] ― -b3- One says also AEtjrt bigulaAmK , or bijaAriyapK , meaning (tropical:) She brought forth a boy, or a girl, after she had despaired of her giving birth to a child. (O, K, TA.)

(A, * K * TA.) ― -b2- [ A protuberance; a knob; a lump. ] ― -b3- A knot in wood, (S, Mgh, O, K,) and the like, (K,) or in other things: (Mgh:) or in the veins of the body: (S:) or a knotted vein in the body; and bujorapN , with which it is coupled, “ a knotted vein in the belly, ” particularly: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) or the former, a thing that collects in the body, like a ganglion ( siloEap ); (As, O, TA;) and the latter signifies the like: (As, TA:) or, as some say, EujarN , which is the pl., signifies the vertebræ of the back: (IAth, TA:) or EujorapN signifies a tumour, or swelling, or an inflation, in the back; and bujorapN , the like in the navel. (TA.) [See also bujorapN .] ― -b4- Hence, one says, *akara Eujarahu wabujarahu (tropical:) He mentioned his vices, or faults, which no one knew save he who tried him, or tested him: (TA:) or his external and internal conditions; what he showed and what he concealed. (IAth, TA.) And A^afaDayotu A_ilayohi biEujariY wabujariY (tropical:) I revealed to him my vices, or faults, by reason of my confidence in him: (A 'Obeyd, O, TA:) or I acquainted him with my whole state, or case; not concealing from him anything thereof. (As, TA.) And A^uHad~ivuhu biEujariY wabujariY (tropical:) I relate to him my vices, or faults. (TA.) And ya$okuw Eujarahu wabujarahu (tropical:) He complains of his vices, or faults, or the like: and of his sorrows: and of what is apparent and what is concealed. (K, * TA. [In the CK, Aubodira is put by mistake for A^ubodiYa .]) One says also, jaA='a fulaAnN biAlEujari waAlbujari (assumed tropical:) i. e. [ Such a one uttered ] falsehood: or a great, or terrible, thing. (Fr, TA.) [See, again, bujorapN .] ― -b5- EujorapN also signifies The mark made upon the waist by the running string of the drawers. (A, TA.) To this a poet likens the mark made by a blunt sword. (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA.) ― -b6- And one says, Als~ayofN fiY firinodihi EujarN [ The sword has, in its diversified wavy marks, what resemble knots ]. (TA.)

definition: [ A species of melon: accord.
sourceDefinition: [ A species of melon: accord. to Forskål, (Flora Aegypt. Arab., pp. lxxvi. and 168,) this name and Ebdl~AwY are both applied to the cucumis chate: but accord. to Delile, (Floræ Aegypt. Illustr., no. 922,) the latter name is thus applied; and Ejwr (written by him as though it were Eaj~uwr , but it is without teshdeed,) is the name of the fruit of this species of cucumis while immature; so too says 'Abd-El-Lateef: (see De Sacy's Transl. and Notes, pp. 35 and 127; and p. 54 of the Ar. Text edited by White:) I have, however, found the name Eajuwr to be commonly applied to a species different from the Eabodal~aAwiY~ , (which is also called Eabodal~iY~ , see art. Ebd ,) as Sonnini asserts it to be, (in his Travels in Upper and Lower Egypt, pp. 574 and 636 of the Engl. Transl., 4to., London, 1800,) and differing therefrom in shape, being, as he describes it, in some instances round, in some instances oval, and in others much elongated: the name is probably derived from the Greek ἀγγούριον (in modern Greek ἀγγοῦρι ), signifying the “ water-melon ”]: it is said in the Msb that qiv~aA=' is a name of what the [common] people call xiyaAr and Eajuwr and faq~uws : but it is said [by some, not by the author of the Msb,] that Eajuwr signifies large qiv~aA=' [q. v.]. (TA in art. qvA^ .)

(O.) -A2- Also both words, (K,) or, accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, the latter, (O,) Custom, habit, or wont: (O, K:) but app. mistranscribed for EariydN . (TA in art. ESd .)

definition: A booth, or shed, or thing constructed for shade, ( miZal~apN ,) mostly made of canes, or reeds;
sourceDefinition: A booth, or shed, or thing constructed for shade, ( miZal~apN ,) mostly made of canes, or reeds; (K;) and sometimes, (TA,) made of palm-sticks, over which is thrown vumaAm [ a species of panic grass ]; (Mgh, TA:) as described by Az, on the authority of the Arabs; (TA;) and such is meant by the Earo$ of Moses: (Mgh:) a thing resembling a house, or tent, made of palm-sticks, over which is put vumaAm ; as also ↓ Eariy$N : (Msb:) a booth, or shed, syn. xayomapN , (K, TA,) made of wood and vmAn ; (TA;) as also ↓ Eariy$N ; (S, A, * O, K;) and such is meant by the ↓ Eariy$ of Moses; (A;) and sometimes the ↓ Eariy$ was made of palm-sticks, with vumaAm thrown over them: (TA:) both signify a thing, (S, O,) or a house, or the like, (K,) used for shade: (S, O, K:) pl. of the former, Euruw$N (ISd, Mgh, Msb, K) and Euru$N and A^aEoraA$N [which is a pl. of pauc.] and Eira$apN : (K:) or Euru$N is pl. of ↓ Eariy$N , (S, ISd, O, Msb,) not of Earo$N : (ISd:) or it is also pl. of ↓ Eariy$N : (K:) and Euruw$N is also a pl. of ↓ Euro$N , which is a pl. of ↓ Eariy$N . (L.) Hence The houses of Mekkeh, (S, A, Mgh, O, Msb,) in which the needy of its inhabitants dwelt, (Mgh,) or its ancient houses, (K,) were called AlEuruw$u , (S, A, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and AlEuru$u , (S, Msb,) and ↓ AlEuro$u ; (O, K;) because they were of poles, or sticks, set up, and shaded over: (S, O, Msb:) or Mekkeh itself was called ↓ AlEuro$u : (Az, O, L, K:) or it was called AlEaro$u , with fet-h, and ↓ AlEariy$u : (Az, L, K:) and its houses were called ↓ AlEuro$u , and AlEuruw$u . (K.) And hence, (S, O, Msb,) the saying in a trad., (S, O,) i. e., the saying of Saad, (K, TA,) when he heard that Mo'áwiyeh forbade the performing conjointly the greater and minor pilgrimages, (TA,) tamat~aEonaA maEa rasuwli A@ll~`hi Sal~aY A@ll~`hu Ealayohi wasal~ama wafulaAnN kaAfirN biAloEuru$i , (S, O, K, *) or biAloEuruw$i , (S, TA,) i. e., [ We performed conjointly the greater and minor pilgrimages with the Apostle of God, ( God bless and save him, )] when such a one, meaning Mo'áwiyeh, was abiding (O, L, K) in his state of unbelief, (L,) in Mekkeh; (L, K;) i. e. in the houses thereof: (O, L:) or, as some say, was hiding himself in the houses of Mekkeh. (L.) ― -b2- A house [ in an absolute sense ]; a dwelling, or place of abode: (Kr, TA:) pl. Euru$N (TA) [and Euruw$N ]. ― -b3- A [ building of the kind called ] qaSor . (K.) ― -b4- The wood upon which stands the drawer of water: (K:) or a structure of wood built at the head of the well, forming a shade: [pl. Euruw$N :] when the props are pulled away, the Euruw$ fall down. (TA.) [ Earo$N in relation to a well has also another meaning; which see below.] ― -b5- The wooden thing [or trellis ] which serves for the propping of a grape-vine. (TA.) [But this is more commonly called Eariy$N , q. v.] ― -b6- The roof of a house or the like: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) pl. Euruw$N . (A.) So in a trad., where a lamp is mentioned as suspended to the Er$ : (O, TA:) and in another, in which a man relates that he used, when upon his Er$ , to hear the Prophet's reciting [of the Kur-án]. (TA.) And so it has been expl. as occurring in the phrase of the Kur [ii. 261 and xxii. 44], xaAwiyapN EalaY Euruw$ihaA Having fallen down upon its roofs: meaning that its walls were standing when their roofs had become demolished and had fallen to the foundations, and the walls fell down upon the roofs demolished before them: (O, TA:) but some consider ElY as here meaning Eano [from]. (TA.) ― -b7- [Hence, app.,] AlEaro$u is applied to The Earo$ of God, which is not definable: (A, K:) I'Ab is related to have said that the kurosiY~ is the place of the feet and the Earo$ is immeasurable: and it is said in the Mufradát of Er-Rághib that the Earo$ of God is one of the things which mankind know not in reality, but only by name; and it is not as the imaginations of the vulgar hold it to be; [namely, the throne of God; ] for were it so, it would be a support to Him; not supported; whereas God saith [in the Kur., xxxv. 39], “ Verily God holdeth the heavens and the earth, lest they should move from their place; and if they should move from their place, no one would hold them after Him: ” or, as some say, it is the highest sphere; [or the empyrean; ] and the krsY~ is the sphere of the stars: and they adduce as an indication thereof the saying of Mohammad, that the seven heavens and earths, by the side of the krsY~ , are nought but as a ring thrown down in a desert land; and such is the krsY~ with respect to the Earo$ : and this assertion is mentioned in the B, but without approval: (TA:) [it appears, however, to be most commonly accepted:] or a red sapphire, which glistens with the light of the Supreme. (A, K.) [Hence the saying,] mina AlEaro$i A_ilaY Alfaro$i meaning, [ From the highest sphere, or the empyrean, to ] the earth. (A.) ― -b8- Also The sariyr [or throne ] (S, A, O, Msb, K) of a king; (S, A, O, K;) the seat of a sultán; [perhaps as being likened to the Er$ of God; or, more probably, from its being generally surmounted by a canopy; or] because of its height. (Er-Rághib.) [Hence,] the phrase AisotawaY EalaY Earo$ihi means He reigned as king. (A, TA.) ― -b9- And [hence, also,] Certain stars in advance of Als~imaAk AlA^aEozal [which is Spica Virginis ]; (TA;) [app. those meant by what here follows;] Earo$u Als~imaAki signifies four small stars [app. γ, δ, ε, and η , of Virgo, regarded as the seat of Bootes, the principal star of which is called Als~imaAku Alr~aAmiHu , being described as] beneath AlEaw~aA=' [which is a name of Bootes and also of the four stars mentioned above], and also called Eajuzu AlA^asadi [ the rump of Leo, the figure of which was extended by the Arabs far beyond the limits which we assign to it]. (S, O, K.) ― -b10- And Earo$u AljawozaA='i [ The seat of Orion; applied by our astronomers to α of Lepus; but described as] four stars, of which two are on the fore legs and two on the hind legs, of Lepus. (Kzw.) ― -b11- And Eamo$u Alv~aray~aA Certain stars near Alv~uray~aA [or the Pleiades ]. (T, TA.) ― -b12- Earo$N also signifies The jamaAzap ; (O, K, TA;) i. e., the bier of a corpse. (O, TA.) And hence, as some say, the expression in a trad., Aihotaz~a AlEaro$u limawoti saEodi boni muEaA*K , meaning The bier rejoiced [lit. shook ] at the death of Saad Ibn-Mo'ádh; i. e., at carrying him upon it to his place of burial: (O, K, * TA:) but there are other explanations, for which see art. hz . (TA.) ― -b13- The wood with which a well is cased after it has been cased with stones (S, O, K) in its lowest part (S, O) to the height of the stature of a man: (S, O, K:) pl. Euruw$N . (S, O.) [Another meaning of the same word in relation to a well has been mentioned before.] ― -b14- (assumed tropical:) The nest of a bird, such as is built in a tree, (K,) [app. as being likened to a booth.] ― -b15- The angle, or corner, or strongest side, syn. rukon , (Ks, Zj, K,) of a house, (Ks, Zj,) or [other] thing: (K:) pl. Euruw$N . (Ks, Zj.) Accord. to some, the phrase in the Kur [ii. 261, mentioned above], xaAwiyapN EalaY Euruw$ihaA , means Empty, and fallen to ruin upon its A^arokaAn [or angles, &c.]. (Ks, Zj, O.) ― -b16- [Hence,] (tropical:) The head, or chief, who is the manager or regulator of the affairs, of a people, or company of men: (K:) likened to the Earo$ of a house. (TA.) ― -b17- [Hence also,] (assumed tropical:) The means of support of a thing, or an affair. (A, O, K.) Hence the saying, vul~a Earo$uhu , (O, K,) meaning (tropical:) His means of support became taken away: (TA:) or he perished: (A:) or he was slain; as also ↓ vul~a Euro$uhu : (IDrd, in M, art. vl :) or his might, or power, departed: (TA:) or his affairs, or state, became weak, and his might, or power, departed. (S, O. [See also art. vl .] [For Earo$N also signifies] ― -b18- (tropical:) Might, or power: (Er-Rághib, K:) regal power; sovereignty; dominion: (IAar, Er-Rághib, K:) from the same word as signifying the throne, or seat, of a king. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b19- And The protuberant part (S, O, K) in, (S, O,) or of, (K,) the upper surface of the foot, (S, O, K,) in which are the toes; (S, O, TA;) as also ↓ Euro$N : pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoraA$N and [of mult.] Eira$apN : (O, TA:) and the part between the Eayor [or prominent bone ] and the toes, of the upper surface of the foot; as also ↓ Euro$N : (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, K:) pls. the same as last mentioned above: (K:) or ↓ Euro$N signifies the upper surface of the foot; and its lower surface is called the A^axomaS . (IAar.)

And hence, (S, O, Msb,) the saying in a trad., (S, O,) i. e., the saying of Saad, (K, TA,) when he heard that Mo'áwiyeh forbade the performing conjointly the greater and minor pilgrimages, (TA,) tamat~aEonaA maEa rasuwli A@ll~`hi Sal~aY A@ll~`hu Ealayohi wasal~ama wafulaAnN kaAfirN biAloEuru$i , (S, O, K, *) or biAloEuruw$i , (S, TA,) i. e., [ We performed conjointly the greater and minor pilgrimages with the Apostle of God, ( God bless and save him, )] when such a one, meaning Mo'áwiyeh, was abiding (O, L, K) in his state of unbelief, (L,) in Mekkeh; (L, K;) i. e. in the houses thereof: (O, L:) or, as some say, was hiding himself in the houses of Mekkeh. (L.) ― -b2- A house [ in an absolute sense ]; a dwelling, or place of abode: (Kr, TA:) pl. Euru$N (TA) [and Euruw$N ]. ― -b3- A [ building of the kind called ] qaSor . (K.) ― -b4- The wood upon which stands the drawer of water: (K:) or a structure of wood built at the head of the well, forming a shade: [pl. Euruw$N :] when the props are pulled away, the Euruw$ fall down. (TA.) [ Earo$N in relation to a well has also another meaning; which see below.] ― -b5- The wooden thing [or trellis ] which serves for the propping of a grape-vine. (TA.) [But this is more commonly called Eariy$N , q. v.] ― -b6- The roof of a house or the like: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) pl. Euruw$N . (A.) So in a trad., where a lamp is mentioned as suspended to the Er$ : (O, TA:) and in another, in which a man relates that he used, when upon his Er$ , to hear the Prophet's reciting [of the Kur-án]. (TA.) And so it has been expl. as occurring in the phrase of the Kur [ii. 261 and xxii. 44], xaAwiyapN EalaY Euruw$ihaA Having fallen down upon its roofs: meaning that its walls were standing when their roofs had become demolished and had fallen to the foundations, and the walls fell down upon the roofs demolished before them: (O, TA:) but some consider ElY as here meaning Eano [from]. (TA.) ― -b7- [Hence, app.,] AlEaro$u is applied to The Earo$ of God, which is not definable: (A, K:) I'Ab is related to have said that the kurosiY~ is the place of the feet and the Earo$ is immeasurable: and it is said in the Mufradát of Er-Rághib that the Earo$ of God is one of the things which mankind know not in reality, but only by name; and it is not as the imaginations of the vulgar hold it to be; [namely, the throne of God; ] for were it so, it would be a support to Him; not supported; whereas God saith [in the Kur., xxxv. 39], “ Verily God holdeth the heavens and the earth, lest they should move from their place; and if they should move from their place, no one would hold them after Him: ” or, as some say, it is the highest sphere; [or the empyrean; ] and the krsY~ is the sphere of the stars: and they adduce as an indication thereof the saying of Mohammad, that the seven heavens and earths, by the side of the krsY~ , are nought but as a ring thrown down in a desert land; and such is the krsY~ with respect to the Earo$ : and this assertion is mentioned in the B, but without approval: (TA:) [it appears, however, to be most commonly accepted:] or a red sapphire, which glistens with the light of the Supreme. (A, K.) [Hence the saying,] mina AlEaro$i A_ilaY Alfaro$i meaning, [ From the highest sphere, or the empyrean, to ] the earth. (A.) ― -b8- Also The sariyr [or throne ] (S, A, O, Msb, K) of a king; (S, A, O, K;) the seat of a sultán; [perhaps as being likened to the Er$ of God; or, more probably, from its being generally surmounted by a canopy; or] because of its height. (Er-Rághib.) [Hence,] the phrase AisotawaY EalaY Earo$ihi means He reigned as king. (A, TA.) ― -b9- And [hence, also,] Certain stars in advance of Als~imaAk AlA^aEozal [which is Spica Virginis ]; (TA;) [app. those meant by what here follows;] Earo$u Als~imaAki signifies four small stars [app. γ, δ, ε, and η , of Virgo, regarded as the seat of Bootes, the principal star of which is called Als~imaAku Alr~aAmiHu , being described as] beneath AlEaw~aA=' [which is a name of Bootes and also of the four stars mentioned above], and also called Eajuzu AlA^asadi [ the rump of Leo, the figure of which was extended by the Arabs far beyond the limits which we assign to it]. (S, O, K.) ― -b10- And Earo$u AljawozaA='i [ The seat of Orion; applied by our astronomers to α of Lepus; but described as] four stars, of which two are on the fore legs and two on the hind legs, of Lepus. (Kzw.) ― -b11- And Eamo$u Alv~aray~aA Certain stars near Alv~uray~aA [or the Pleiades ]. (T, TA.) ― -b12- Earo$N also signifies The jamaAzap ; (O, K, TA;) i. e., the bier of a corpse. (O, TA.) And hence, as some say, the expression in a trad., Aihotaz~a AlEaro$u limawoti saEodi boni muEaA*K , meaning The bier rejoiced [lit. shook ] at the death of Saad Ibn-Mo'ádh; i. e., at carrying him upon it to his place of burial: (O, K, * TA:) but there are other explanations, for which see art. hz . (TA.) ― -b13- The wood with which a well is cased after it has been cased with stones (S, O, K) in its lowest part (S, O) to the height of the stature of a man: (S, O, K:) pl. Euruw$N . (S, O.) [Another meaning of the same word in relation to a well has been mentioned before.] ― -b14- (assumed tropical:) The nest of a bird, such as is built in a tree, (K,) [app. as being likened to a booth.] ― -b15- The angle, or corner, or strongest side, syn. rukon , (Ks, Zj, K,) of a house, (Ks, Zj,) or [other] thing: (K:) pl. Euruw$N . (Ks, Zj.) Accord. to some, the phrase in the Kur [ii. 261, mentioned above], xaAwiyapN EalaY Euruw$ihaA , means Empty, and fallen to ruin upon its A^arokaAn [or angles, &c.]. (Ks, Zj, O.) ― -b16- [Hence,] (tropical:) The head, or chief, who is the manager or regulator of the affairs, of a people, or company of men: (K:) likened to the Earo$ of a house. (TA.) ― -b17- [Hence also,] (assumed tropical:) The means of support of a thing, or an affair. (A, O, K.) Hence the saying, vul~a Earo$uhu , (O, K,) meaning (tropical:) His means of support became taken away: (TA:) or he perished: (A:) or he was slain; as also ↓ vul~a Euro$uhu : (IDrd, in M, art. vl :) or his might, or power, departed: (TA:) or his affairs, or state, became weak, and his might, or power, departed. (S, O. [See also art. vl .] [For Earo$N also signifies] ― -b18- (tropical:) Might, or power: (Er-Rághib, K:) regal power; sovereignty; dominion: (IAar, Er-Rághib, K:) from the same word as signifying the throne, or seat, of a king. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b19- And The protuberant part (S, O, K) in, (S, O,) or of, (K,) the upper surface of the foot, (S, O, K,) in which are the toes; (S, O, TA;) as also ↓ Euro$N : pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoraA$N and [of mult.] Eira$apN : (O, TA:) and the part between the Eayor [or prominent bone ] and the toes, of the upper surface of the foot; as also ↓ Euro$N : (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, K:) pls. the same as last mentioned above: (K:) or ↓ Euro$N signifies the upper surface of the foot; and its lower surface is called the A^axomaS . (IAar.)

definition: , (S, K,) or Ald~aAb~apa , (Mgh, Msb,) He rode the horse, or the beast, without a saddle, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, * and Ham p.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) or Ald~aAb~apa , (Mgh, Msb,) He rode the horse, or the beast, without a saddle, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, * and Ham p. 42,) and having nothing beneath him; (Ham:) the verb being of the measure AifoEawoEala , (S, TA,) a measure of which there is no other trans. v. except AiHolawolaY . (TA.) ― -b2- Hence the usage of the verb in the saying of Taäbbata-Sharrà yaZal~u bimawomaApK wayumosiY bigayorihaA jaHiy$FA wayaEoraworiY Zuhuwra AlmahaAliki (assumed tropical:) He passes the day in a waterless desert, and enters upon the evening in another than it, alone, and he ventures upon [ the surfaces of ] the places of perdition without anything to protect him from them. (Ham ubi suprà.) [See also an ex. of the act. part. n. in a verse cited in the second paragraph of art. dwm .] ― -b3- And AErwrY Als~araAbu AlA=kaAma means rakibahaA [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The mirage surmounted the hills, or mounds ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And AErwrY A^amorFA qabiyHFA (assumed tropical:) He ventured upon, or did, an evil, or a foul, thing; (S, K; *) syn. rakibahu , (S,) or A^ataAhu , (K,) or both. (TA.) ― -b5- AErwrY signifies also (assumed tropical:) He journeyed by himself, alone, in the earth, or land. (K.)

definition: and ↓ EaArK Naked, nude, bare, or without clothing;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ EaArK Naked, nude, bare, or without clothing; (S, * MA, Mgh, * Msb, * K, TA;) applied to a man: (Msb, TA:) fem. EuroyaAnapN (S, MA, Mgh, &c.) and ↓ EaAriyapN , (MA, Mgh, Msb, &c.,) applied to a woman: (S, Msb:) the pl. of EuroyaAnN is EuroyaAnuwna ; (K;) and the pl. of ↓ EaArK is EuraApN , (Msb, K,) and that of EaAriyapN is EaAriyaAtN . (Msb.) [Also, sometimes, Bare of clothing, or of his clothes, except one, or more, of his inner garments. ] See also EuroYN . ― -b2- EuroyaAnN applied to sand, (assumed tropical:) An extended and gibbous tract ( naqFA ), or such as is accumulated and congested ( EaqidN , in the CK EaqodN ), of sand, having no trees upon it. (ISd, K, TA.) ― -b3- Applied to a plant, or to herbage, (assumed tropical:) Such as has become apparent. (TA.) ― -b4- EuroyaAnu Aln~ajiY~i is an appellation applied to (assumed tropical:) A wife: but in the A it is implied that it is used as denoting anyone who will not conceal a secret. (TA.) ― -b5- EuroyaAnN applied to a horse signifies (assumed tropical:) Light, or active, and quick; tall; and long in the legs. (K, TA. [Expl. in the K and TA by the words muqal~S Tawiyl ; to which is added in the TA AlqawaAy^im : the first of these words I find written, in copies of the K, only muqal~aS ; but it is correctly muqal~iS .])

definition: (IF, S, O, Msb, K) [generally held to be an inf.
sourceDefinition: (IF, S, O, Msb, K) [generally held to be an inf. n.] and ↓ maEo$aqN [likewise app. an inf. n.] (O, K) Excessive love; (IF, S, O, Msb, K;) [or passionate love; or amorous desire: ] or attackment to women: (IF, Msb:) or the lover's admiration ( Eajab [for Eujobu in the CK is a mistranscription for Eajabu ]) of the beloved; and it may be in chasteness and in immorality; (K;) or Ei$oqN may be in chasteness and Hub~N may be in immorality: (TA:) or blindness of the sense to the faults, or defects, of the beloved: or a disease of the nature of melancholia ( maraDN wasowaAsiY~N ), which one procures to himself by making his thought to exercise absolute power over the approval of certain forms: (K:) Th, being asked respecting AlHub~ and AlEi$oq , which of them is the more commendable, said, AlHub~ , because in AlEi$oq is excess: (TA:) [see also Hub~N :] Ibn-Seenà, [whom we commonly call Avicenna,] in a treatise on AlEi$oq , [regarding it as meaning natural propension, ] says that it is not peculiar to the human species, but pervades all existing things of the celestial and the elemental and the vegetable and the mineral and the animal, and that its meaning is not perceived nor known, and is rendered more obscure by explanation thereof: (MF, TA:) it is said in the A that AlEi$oq is derived from AlEa$aqapu , which means the [plant commonly called] labolaAb , because it twines upon trees, and cleaves to them. (TA.)

definition: Loving excessively;
sourceDefinition: Loving excessively; [or passionately; ] &c.; (Msb, K;) [or an excessive, or a passionate, lover; ] as also ↓ EaA$iqapN : (TA:) the former applied to a man and to a woman, (Msb, K,) and EaA$iqapN also is applied to a woman, (K:) they said AimoraA^apN EaA$iqN lizawojihaA [ A woman excessively, or passionately, loving to her husband ]; (Fr, S, O;) and sometimes they said EaA$iqapN : (O:) pl. Eu$~aAqN (TA) [and Eu$~aqN , mentioned in the O as an epithet applied to eyes ( Euyuwn ), by Ru-beh]: it is asserted that the EaA$iq is thus called from AlEa$aqapu meaning the labolaAbap , because of his becoming dried up: (O, TA:) or from Ea$iqa bihi , because of his cleaving to the object of his love. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] EaA$iqu AlA^abokaAri an appellation of The insect called HuroquwS [q. v.]; because of its entering into the faroj of the virgin girl. (IB, TA voce HrqwS .)

definition: A winnowing-fork;
sourceDefinition: A winnowing-fork; i. e. the wooden implement (S, ISd, K) with prongs (ISd, K) with which wheat is winnowed: (S, ISd, K:) and EaZomN is a dial. var. thereof: (AHn, TA:) pl. A^aEoDimapN and EuDomN , [the former of pauc. and the latter of mult.,] (K, TA,) both anomalous; the true state of the case being that they formed from EaDomN the pl. EiDaAmN ; and from this, A^aEoDimapN and EuDumN , [of which latter, EuDomN is app. a contraction,] like A^amovilapN and muvulN pls. of mivaAlN . (TA.) ― -b2- And The board, (S, K,) i. e. the broad board, (TA,) of the plough, at the head of which is the iron [or share ] (S, K, TA) that cleaves the earth: and so EaZomN , accord. to AHn. (TA.) ― -b3- And The handle, or part that is grasped by the hand, of a bow: (S, K:) and EaZomN is a dial. var. thereof: (AHn, TA:) pl. EiDaAmN . (K.) ― -b4- And The [ part of the tail called ] Easiyb [q. v.], (S, K, TA,) or the Eukowap [or root of the tail where it is bare of hair, S in art. Ekw ], (TA,) of the camel, (S, TA,) or of the horse, (ISd, TA,) or of both: (K:) as also ↓ EiDaAmN , (K,) of which EiSaAmN is a dial. var.: (TA: [but see the latter:]) pl. A^aEoDimapN (S, TA) and EuDumN , [both, accord. to analogy, of the latter sing.,] the former of pauc. and the latter of mult. (TA.) ― -b5- And A line, or streak, in a mountain, differing from the rest in colour. (K, TA.) -A2- Also Mountain goats. (K.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ AETlhu signify the same [app. in all the senses assigned to the former]. (O.) ― -b2- 'Áïsheh is related, in a trad., to have said respecting a woman who had died, EaT~iluwhaA , meaning Divest ye her of her ornaments. (S, O.) ― -b3- [Hence,] ET~l Alqawosa , inf. n. taEoTiylN , He divested the bow of its string. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence likewise, the inf. n.] Alt~aEoTiylu signifies [also] The rendering vacant, void, or unoccupied, (K, TA,) a place of abode, and the like. (TA.) And The leaving a thing untended, unminded, or neglected. (K, TA. [ DiyAEFA in the CK is a mistake for DayaAEFA .]) One says of the frontier of a hostile country, EuT~ila , meaning It was left without any to defend it. (TA.) And of subjects one says, EuT~iluwA , meaning They were left without any one to govern them. (TA.) One says also, EaT~alotu AlA_ibila , inf. n. as above, I left the camels without a pastor to tend them. (Msb.) waA_i*aA AlEi$aAru EuT~ilato , in the Kur lxxxi. 4, means And when the pregnant camels [ ten months gone with young ] shall be left without a pastor, or without being milked [?]; (Jel;) by reason of the terrors of the hour; (O;) i. e. by men's having their minds occupied by the terrors of the day of resurrection. (TA.) And EuT~ilato is said of lands of seed-produce as meaning They were left uncultivated. (TA.) ― -b5- Alt~aEoTiylu signifies also Alt~aforiygu [as meaning The making, or leaving, vacant from any work, occupation, employment, or use; free therefrom; unoccupied; or unemployed ]. (S, O, K.) One says, EaT~alotu AlA^ajiyra I made the hired man to be unoccupied. (Msb.) And ET~l Alxayola mina Algazowi (S and K in art. bhw ) [ He freed the horses from service in warfare; ] he did not go to war upon the horses. (TA in that art.) ― -b6- [Also The assertion of the tenet, or tenets, of the muEaT~il , q. v.] ― -b7- And taEoTiylu AlHuduwdi means The not inflicting the [ punishments termed ] Hdwd upon him to whom they are due. (TA.)

definition: One who asserts that the universe is devoid of an artificer who constructed it skilfully and adorned it: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [but] the muEaT~ilap of the Arabs were of different sorts: one sort of them...
sourceDefinition: One who asserts that the universe is devoid of an artificer who constructed it skilfully and adorned it: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [but] the muEaT~ilap of the Arabs were of different sorts: one sort of them disacknowledged the Creator, and the raising and restoring to life, and asserted that nature is that which brings to life and time is that which brings to nought: another sort of them acknowledged the Creator, and the beginning of creation, but disacknowledged the raising and restoring to life: and another sort of them acknowledged the Creator, and the begining of creation, and a mode of restoration to life, but disacknowledged the apostles, and worshipped idols, and asserted them to be their intercessors with God in the life to come, and performed pilgrimage to them, and sacrificed victims to them, and offered offerings, and sought to advance themselves in their favour by means of religious rites and ceremonies, and legalized [ certain things ] and prohibited [ others ]; and these were the generality of the Arabs, except a small portion of them. (Esh-Shahristánee.)

sourceDefinition: What comes forth from the belly of the child (S, Msb, K) before he eats, (S,) or when he is born, (Msb, K,) black and viscous as though it were glue; (Msb;) and likewise from the mare's foal, and the young ass, and the young camel, and the kid; (ISd, TA;) or what comes forth from the lamb or kid, and the mare's foal, is called radajN : (S, TA:) and Az states that it is said to be what comes forth from the belly of the fœtus, inclosed in the [ membrane called ] HuwalaA=' [q. v.]; a thing [or substance ] that comes forth from its anus while it is in the belly of its mother, part of it black and part of it yellow: (TA:) pl. A^aEoqaA='N . (Az, K, TA.) A^aHoraSu mino kalobK EalaY EiqoYi SabiY~K is a prov. [meaning More eager than a dog for the feces of a young child ]. (S.) ― -b2- Also A youngling, or young infant: whence the saying of Z, ↓ fulaAnN lahu EiqoyaAni walayosa Einodahu AlEiqoyaAnu i. e. Such a one has two younglings, or young infants, but gold is not in his possession. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: I milked the she-camel in the morning and the evening and the middle of the day: (Lh, O, TA:) in the K, erroneously, EaAl~ati Aln~aAqapu [as meaning the she-camel was milked at those times ]: (TA:) and the subst. is ↓ EilaAlN : (K: [but there is no reason why this should not be regarded as a reg. inf. n.:]) Lh cites this verse, (O,) of an Arab of the desert, (TA,) AaloEanozu taEolamu A^an~iY laA A^ukar~imuhaA Eani AlEilaAli walaA Eano qidori A^aDoyaAfiY [ The she-goat knows that I will not preserve her from the milking in the morning and the evening and the middle of the day nor from the cookingpot of my guests ]: (O:) or, accord. to Az, EilaAlN signifies the milking after milking, before the udder requires it by the abundance of the milk. (TA.) [See also 6.]

definition: I brought, or sent, back the camels from the water (S, O, K) after they had satisfied their thirst, (O,) or before they had satisfied their thirst: (S, K:) or, (S, O, K,) [if the latter is meant,] accord.
sourceDefinition: I brought, or sent, back the camels from the water (S, O, K) after they had satisfied their thirst, (O,) or before they had satisfied their thirst: (S, K:) or, (S, O, K,) [if the latter is meant,] accord. to some of the etymologists, (S, O,) it is with g ; (S, O, K; [see 4 in art. gl ;]) as though it were from the meaning of “ thirsting; ” but the former is what has been heard; (S, O;) and it means I gave the camels to drink the second draught, or watered them the second time, and then brought them, or sent them, back from the water, having their thirst satisfied; and thus, too, means AlA_ibila ↓ Eal~alatu ; the contr. of A^agolalonuhaA . (TA.) See also 1, first sentence. ― -b2- And AEl~ Alqawomu The people, or party, were, or became, persons whose camels had drunk the second time. (S, O, K. *) -A2- AEl~hu A@ll~`hu God caused him to be diseased, sick, or ill; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ Eal~ahu , aor. . (Msb.) One says, laA A^aEal~aka A@ll~`hu , meaning May God not smite thee with a disease, a sickness, or an illness. (S, O.) ― -b2- And AEl~hu signifies also He made him, or pronounced him, to have an excuse ( jaEalahu *aA Eil~apK ): whence A_iEolaAlaAtu AlfuqahaA='i [ The excusings of the lawyers ]. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: He diverted himself, (S,) or occupied himself so as to divert himself, (K,) and (S, in the K “ or ”) contented, or satisfied, himself, or he was, or became diverted, &c., with it; (S, K;) as also ↓ AEtl~ : (K:) as, for instance, with a portion of food, [ so that the craving of his stomach became allayed, ] before the [morning-meal called] gadaA=' ; (M voce sulofapN , and K voce lumojapN , &c.;) and as a beast does with the cud: (TA:) he occupied himself so as to divert himself, and fed [or sustained ] himself, with it: (Har p. 23:) and he whiled away his time with it. definition: and laEal~a (S, O, Mughnee, K) are dial.
sourceDefinition: and laEal~a (S, O, Mughnee, K) are dial. vars.; or the former is the original, the l being augmentative, (S, O, Mughnee,) prefixed for the purpose of corroboration: the meaning is expectation of a thing hoped for or feared; (S, O;) importing hope, or eager desire, and fear, or caution: (S, O, K:) each is a particle, like A_in~a and layota and kaA^an~a and l`kin~a : (S, O:) and like EasaY [q. v.] in meaning; but like A_in~a in government; (Mughnee;) governing the subject in the accus. case, and the predicate in the nom.: one says, Eal~aka tafoEalu [ Maybe, or perhaps, thou wilt do such a thing], and Eal~iY A^afoEalu [ May-be I shall do ], and laEal~iY A^afoEalu ; and sometimes they said, Eal~aniY and laEal~aniY ; (S, O;) and one says also ↓ Ealo and ↓ laEalo , with the l quiescent, and ↓ Ealoka and ↓ laEaloka : (O:) [and accord. to general usage, one says, laEal~a zayodFA qaAy^imN May-be Zeyd is standing: ] and the tribe of 'Okeyl made each to govern the subject in the gen. case, (S, O, Mughnee,) saying, laEal~a zayodK qaAy^imN ; (S, O;) and allowed the pronouncing Eal~i and laEal~i : (Mughnee:) sometimes its subject is suppressed, as in Eal~a A^ano A^ataqad~ama , meaning laEal~aniY A^ano A^ataqad~ama [ May-be I shall precede ]: (Ham p. 517:) the Koofees allow the mansoob aor. [immediately] after, on the authority of the reading of Hafs, [in the Kur xl. 38,] laEal~iY A^aboluga AlA^asobaAba [ May-be I may reach the places of ascent, or the regions, or tracts, of the heavens]. (Mughnee.) Other dial. vars. of Eal~ are mentioned in art. lEl [q. v.]. (K.)

definition: A [ single ] second draught.
sourceDefinition: A [ single ] second draught. (Mgh.) ― -b2- And hence, (Mgh,) A woman's fellow-wife; her husband's wife: (Mgh, Msb, * K:) or, as some say, a step-mother: but the former is the more correct meaning: (Mgh:) pl. Eal~aAtN . (Msb.) Whence, banuw AlEal~aAti The sons of one father by different mothers: as though, when he added by marriage a second wife to the first, he took a second draught. (S, * Mgh, O, * Msb, * K. *) A^awolaAdu AlA^axoyaAfi means the contr. of this: and A^awolaAdu AlA^aEoyaAni , the sons of the same father and mother. (Msb.) Accord. to IB, one says, humaA A^axawaAni mino Dar~atayoni [They two are brothers from two fellow-wives]; but they did not say, mino Dar~apK : and accord. to ISh, one says, humo banuw Eal~apK and A^awolaAdu Eal~apK . (TA.) And it is said in a trad., AlA^anobiyaA='u banuw Eal~aAti , (Mgh,) or A^awolaAdu Eal~aAtK , (TA,) meaning The prophets are of different mothers, but of one religion: (T, Mgh, TA:) or of one faith, but of different religious laws or ordinances. (Nh, TA.) -A2- See also EulaAlapN .

definition: An accident that befalls an object and causes its state, or condition, to become altered.
sourceDefinition: An accident that befalls an object and causes its state, or condition, to become altered. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (TA,) A disease, sickness, or malady; (S, O, K, TA;) because, by its befalling, the state becomes altered from strength to weakness; so says El-Munáwee in the “ Tow- keef: ” (TA:) or a disease that diverts [ from the ordinary occupations; app. regarded as being from what next follows]: pl. EilalN (Msb) [and Eil~aAtN ]. ― -b3- Also An accident, or event, that diverts the person to whom it occurs from his course, (S, O, K,) or from the object of his want: (M:) as though it became a second occupation hindering him from his former occupation. (S, O.) ― -b4- And [hence,] an excuse; an apology; a plea whereby one excuses himself. (TA.) Hence, (K, * TA,) laAtaEodamu xaroqaA='u Eil~apF [expl. in art. xrq ]. (K, TA.) sourceDefinition: (S, K) and ↓ taEil~apN (S, * K) and ↓ Eal~apN , (K, TA,) with fet-h, (TA, [in the CK AlEil~apu is put for AlEal~apu ,]) A thing with which a person, (S, K,) or a child, (TA,) is diverted, or occupied so as to be diverted, and contented, or satisfied, (S, K, TA,) such as talk, and singing, and food, &c., (Har p. 308,) [or such as a small quantity of food by which the craving of his stomach is allayed, ] in order that he may be quiet. (TA.) It is said in a trad., accord. to different relations thereof, that dates are the ↓ taEil~ap of the child or of the guest. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, the first, accord. to the copies of the K, What is drawn from the udder after the first fiyqap : but accord. to IAar, what is drawn from the udder before the first fiyqap [or milk that collects in the udder between two milkings ], and before the second fyqp collects: also termed EuraAkapN and dulaAkapN : (TA:) [or] the milking that is between two milkings: (S, O:) [or] it signifies also the middle milking of the camel that is milked in the first part and the middle and the last part of the day: (K:) or, as some say, the milk that she excerns [ into her udder ] after the milking of the copious flow thereof. (TA.) ― -b3- And A remaining portion of milk (S, O, K, TA) in the udder: (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) of other things: [for instance,] (tropical:) of the course [ of a beast ]: (K:) (tropical:) of the running of a horse; (S, O, TA;) the former portion whereof is termed budaAhapN : (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) of anything: (S, K:) as (tropical:) of the flesh of a sheep or goat: and (tropical:) of the strength of an old man. (TA.)

(K.)

definition: A pool of water left by a torrent, white, and flowing in a regular, or continuous, course, one portion following another: (As, O, K, TA:) or, accord.
sourceDefinition: A pool of water left by a torrent, white, and flowing in a regular, or continuous, course, one portion following another: (As, O, K, TA:) or, accord. to Suh, in the R, [simply] a pool of water left by a torrent; so called because it waters the ground a second time ( yaEul~u AlA^aroDa bimaAy^ihi [after its having been watered by the rain]): pl. yaEaAliylu . (TA.) ― -b2- And A dye ( Sibog ) that is imbided ( Eul~a ) one time after another: (O, K:) or, accord. to 'Abd-El-Lateef El-Baghdádee, a garment, or piece of cloth, dyed, and dyed again. (TA.) ― -b3- Accord. to AA, [app. as applied to camels,] yaEaAliylu signifies That have drunk one time after another; and has no sing.: but it is said on other authority to signify that go away at random to pasture ( Aal~atiY tahomiY ) one time after another; and to have for its sing. yaEoluwlN : and some say that it signifies such as are excessive in respect of whiteness. (TA.) ― -b4- Also, the sing., Rain after rain: (AO, O, K:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b5- And the pl., (S, M, O, TA,) [accord. to the context in the K the sing., which is clearly wrong,] Bubbles ( HabaAb , M, K, TA, [in the CK HubAb ,] and nuf~aAxaAt , S, O, K, [both, I think, evidently meaning thus,]) upon water; (S, M, O, K;) said to be from the falling of rain; and to be used in a verse of Kaab Ibn-Zuheyr for *aAtu yaEaAliyla as meaning having bubbles: (TA:) sing. as above. (O.) ― -b6- And Clouds disposed one above another; (S, O;) sing. as above: (S:) or [simply] clouds; so in the R; to which ISd adds containing rain: (TA:) or white clouds; (K, TA; a meaning assigned in the K to the sing.;) but this is said by Niftaweyh in explanation of the phrase biyDN yaEaAliylu in a verse of Kaab Ibn-Zuheyr to which reference has been made above: (TA:) or [the sing. signifies] a white portion of clouds. (M, K.) ― -b7- The pl. is also said to signify Lofty mountains; and Suh adds, from the upper parts of which water descends. (TA.) -A2- Also, the sing., A camel having two humps. (IAar, O, K.) ― -b2- And A camel such as is termed A^afiyl [q. v.]. (O.)

definition: A certain tree of El-Hijáz, having a red fruit, to which are likened the dyed fingers or ends of fingers: (IAar, K:) in the “ Nawádir ” said to be sappy, or tender, branches, that grow upon the...
sourceDefinition: A certain tree of El-Hijáz, having a red fruit, to which are likened the dyed fingers or ends of fingers: (IAar, K:) in the “ Nawádir ” said to be sappy, or tender, branches, that grow upon the trunks of the [ trees called ] EiDaAh , not resembling the other branches thereof, red in colour, the upper parts of the blossoms of which divide into four divisions, like a branch of an A^araAkap [n. un. of A^araAkN , q. v.]; coming forth in winter and in summer: (IDrd, TA:) or a species of trees having tender branches, to which are likened the fingers, or the ends of the fingers, of girls, or young women: (S:) in the “ Book of Plants ” [of AHn] said to be a small tree that grows in the midst, or interior part, of the samurap [or gum-acacia-tree ], having a red fruit: (TA:) or, accord. to AA, the [ fruit called ] zuEoruwr [q. v.]: (TA, and so in a copy of the S:) or, (S, K, TA,) as AO says, (S, TA,) the extremities of the Syrian xar~uwb [or locust-tree ]: (S, K, TA:) and he says that a verse of En-Nábighah is recited thus: bimuxaD~abK raxoSK kaA^an~a banaAnahu EanamN EalaY A^agoSaAnihi lamo yuEoqadi [ With a dyed member ( EuDowK being understood, instead of kaf~K , because the latter is fem.,) soft, or tender, as though its fingers, or its fingers' ends, were 'anam upon their branches, not yet compactly organized ]; which shows that it means a plant, not a worm: (S, TA:) [for] it is said to signify a species of red worm, found in sand: (Ham p. 288, in which are other explanations, nearly agreeing with some here:) or, as some say, the fruit of the Eawosaj [or box-thorn ], which is red, and then becomes black when thoroughly ripe; therefore En-Nábighah says lamo yuEoqad , meaning that had not yet become ripe: (IB, TA; and also inserted in the text of a copy of the S:) and, (K, TA,) as AHn says in one instance, (TA,) threads [or tendrils ] by means of which the vine clings to its trellises: (K, TA:) and (accord. to Lth, TA) the thorns of the TaloH [or acacia gummifera ]; (K, TA;) but this is said by Az to be incorrect: (TA:) [see also a hemistich cited voce TarafN :] the n. un. is ↓ EanamapN . (K.)

definition: , (S, O, L, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, L, Msb, K,) aor. yaEowaju , (TA,) inf. n. EawajN (S, O, L, Msb) and EiwajN , (L,) or the latter is a simple subst.; (S, O, K;) and ↓ AiEowaj~a , [which is more common,] inf. n. AiEowijaAjN ; (S, O, L, Msb, K;) and ↓ AnEAj ; and ↓ tEw~j ; (L;) It was, or became, crooked, curved, bent, winding, wry, contorted, distorted, or uneven: (L:) or [ Eawija and] ↓ AEwj~ , it was, or became, so of itself; and [↓ AnEAj and] ↓ tEw~j , it was, or became, so by the operation of an external agent; (L, Msb;) as is said by Az: (L:) ↓ AnEAj is quasi-pass. of Eujotuhu ; (L;) and ↓ tEw~j is quasi-pass. of Eaw~ajotuhu : (Az, S, O, L, Msb, K:) and EawajN and EiwajN are said to be used in relation to different things: (S, O, L, Msb, K, &c.:) [for instance,] one says, Eawija AlEuwdu , inf. n. EawajN , The wood, or stick, was, or became, crooked, curved, bent, or distorted: and Eawija AlA^amoru , inf. n. EiwajN , The affair was, or became, difficult, arduous, or troublesome. (MA.) [See EawajN below.] ― -b2- laA Eiwaja lahu , in the Kur xx. 107, means There shall be no evading it. (Jel.) ― -b3- Eujotu A_ilayohi , aor. A^aEuwju , inf. n. EiyaAjN and EiwajN , I turned, or inclined, towards it; namely, a place of abode. (L.) And Ealayohi ↓ AnEAj He turned, or inclined, towards it, or him. (S, O.) And ↓ AnEAjt and ↓ tEw~jt , said of a she-camel, She turned aside; or became turned aside; the former quasi-pass. of EaAjahaA ; and the latter, of Eaw~ajahaA . (TA.) ― -b4- EAj bihi He inclined, and came to him, or came to him and alighted at his abode as a guest: and he passed by him. (L.) And Eujotu biAlmakaAni , aor. A^aEuwju , (S, O, K, *) inf. n. EawojN and maEaAjN ; (K;) and ↓ Ew~jtu ; (TA;) I remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, in the place. (S, O, K. *) And EAj Ealayohi He stopped, or paused, at it. (S, * O, * K, * TA.) A poet says, EujonaA EalaY raboEi salomaY A^aY~a taEoriyji [ We stopped at the abode of Selmà, with what a staying! ]: putting tEryj [in some copies of the S tEwyj ] in the place of Eawoj because their meaning is one. (S, O, TA.) ― -b5- fulaAnN maA yaEuwju Eano $aYo'K Such a one does not revert from, or relinquish, anything. (IAar, S, O, K. *) ― -b6- Accord. to AA, [the inf. n.] EiyaAjN signifies The returning to that upon which one had been intent, or attent, or employed. (O and TA in art. Eyj .) -A2- Eujotuhu : see 2. ― -b2- Eujotu AlbaEiyra , (S, A, * O, K, *) and Eujotu raA^osa AlbaEiyri , (L,) aor. A^aEuwjuhu , inf. n. EawojN (S, O, L) and maEaAjN , (S, O,) I turned the camel's head by means of the nose-rein: (S, A, * O, L, K: *) and in like manner one says of a horse: and EAj naAqatahu , and ↓ Ew~jhA , He turned aside his she-camel. (TA.) And EAj raA^osahu A_ilaY AlmaroA^api (O and TA from a trad.) He inclined his head towards the woman, and looked towards her. (TA.) And AlmaroA^apu taEuwju raA^osahaA A_ilaY DajiyEihaA [ The woman turns her head towards her bedfellow ]. (TA.) And EAj Eunuqahu , inf. n. EawojN , He inclined, or bent, his neck. (TA.) And Eujo lisaAnaka Ean~iY walaA tukoviro [ Turn, or withhold, thy tongue from me, and do not multiply words]. (A.) And bihi AlT~ariyqu ↓ Eaw~aja [ The road led him, or turned him, aside ]. (K in explanation of Haw~aja .) ― -b3- maA A^aEuwju bikalaAmihi I do not pay regard, or attention, to his speech, (ISk, S in art. Eyj , A, * and O,) is a phrase of the Benoo-Asad, who take it from Eujotu Aln~aAqapa : (ISk, S, O:) others say maA A^aEiyju . (O.) And one says, maA Eujotu biHadiyvihi [ I did not pay regard to his discourse ]. (A.) ― -b4- Eujotuhu biAlmakaAni I made him to remain, stay, dwell, or abide, in the place: the verb being trans. as well as intrans. (S, O.)

sourceDefinition: , as an epithet applied to a she-camel, Pliable; syn. lay~inapN AlA^aEoTaAfi , or lay~inapu AlAinoEiTaAfi , accord. to different copies of the K; and by the latter words is expl. (but not in the K) ↓ EaAy^ijapN , as so applied: in the L, EaAjN is expl. as meaning tractable, submissive, or manageable; syn. mi*oEaAnN : (TA:) or mi*oEaAnu Als~ayori lay~inapu AlAinoEiTaAfi (thus in the O:) and it is said to be without a parallel in respect of the dropping of the [fem. termination] p , whether its original measure be faEilN or faAEilN [?]. (TA.) -A2- Also [ Ivory; ] elephant's bone; (S, O, K;) or [rather] only elephant's tusk; (Lth, Msb, TA;) thus say ISd and Kz: (TA:) n. un. with p [signifying a piece of ivory ]: (S, O:) of its properties are these: that if seed-produce or trees be fumigated with it, worms will not approach them; and the woman who drinks of it every day two drachms with water and honey, if compressed after seven days, conceives. (K.) ― -b2- And Tortoise-shell; syn. *abolN [q. v.]; (O, K;) i. e. (O) the back [or shell ] of the sea-tortoise [or turtle ]: (O, Msb:) i. q. masakN : (Sh, L:) or a thing that is made from the back of the sea-tortoise: (L:) and it is said that the Arabs called any [ sort of ] bone by this name: n. un. with p . (TA.) The Prophet is related to have had a comb of EAj , i. e. *abol : (L:) and he is said to have ordered to purchase for Fátimeh a pair of bracelets of EAj , by which he meant not what is turned of elephants' tusks, for their tusks are mayotap , [i. e. they are taken from an animal of which the flesh is unlawful food,] but *bl : (O, * L, Msb: *) the EAj of the elephant is impure accord. to EshSháfi'ee, but pure accord. to Aboo-Haneefeh. (L.) ― -b3- Also Bracelets of EAj , as distinguished from *abol , [i. e. of ivory: and probably of tortoise-shell also:] (ISh:) n. un. with p . definition: and ↓ EiwajN [are inf.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ EiwajN [are inf. ns. of Eawija , q. v., or the latter is a simple subst.; and both, used as simple substs.,] signify Crookedness, curvity, a bending, a winding, wryness, contortion, distortion, or unevenness: (L:) or the former is peculiar to objects of the sight, as bodies; and the latter, to what are not seen, as opinion, and a saying, and religion: or, as some say, the latter is used in both of these cases; but the distinction is more common: (IAth, TA:) AZ makes the same distinction; but adds that some of the Arabs used the latter word in relation to a road: (Msb:) accord. to ISk, (S, O,) the former is in anything erect, (S, O, K,) or in anything that was erect and has inclined, (TA,) as a wall, (S, O, K, TA,) and a stick, (S, O, Msb,) or a staff, (K, TA,) and a spear; (TA;) and the latter, in land, or ground, and in religion, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) and in means of subsistence: (S, O:) in land, or ground, the latter means unevenness; thus in the Kur xx. 106: in a road, deflection; as also EawajN : in religion, and in natural disposition, corruptness, or deviation from rectitude: (TA:) and EawajN , (S, O, TA, [thus accord. to both of my copies of the S,]) or EiwajN , (accord. to a copy of the A, [which I incline to regard as the right, in consideration of its consistency with explanations here preceding, notwithstanding the apparent preponderance of authority in favour of EawajN ,]) in a man, signifies evilness of natural disposition: (S, A, O: [and so, app., hawajN :]) or EawajN , with fet-h to the E , as an inf. n., signifies the being evil in natural disposition. (KL.)

definition: Crooked, curved, bent, or bending, winding, wry, contorted, distorted, or uneven: (S, * O, * L, Msb:) and ↓ muEowaj~N , [or this and the former also,] crooked, curved, &c.
sourceDefinition: Crooked, curved, bent, or bending, winding, wry, contorted, distorted, or uneven: (S, * O, * L, Msb:) and ↓ muEowaj~N , [or this and the former also,] crooked, curved, &c., of itself: fem. of the former EawojaA='u : (L, Msb:) and pl. EuwjN . (L.) One says ↓ EaSFA muEowaj~apN [ A crooked, or crooking, staff or stick ]; but not miEowaj~apN , with kesr to the m : (S, O:) or, accord. to ISk, one says the former; but not ↓ muEaw~ajapN , with fet-h to the E and teshdeed to the w ; though analogy does not forbid this, as it is allowable to say Eaw~ajahaA : accord. to As, one should not say ↓ muEaw~ajN , with teshdeed to the w , except in applying it to a stick, or in another sense expl. below: Az says that this word is allowable as signifying rendered crooked or curved &c. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AlEawojaA='u signifies The bow. (S, A, K.) ― -b3- And EawojaA='u applied to a woman, Inclining, or bending, towards her child, to suckle it. (TA.) And, so applied, That has become crooked by reason of leanness and hunger. (Ham p. 744.) And, applied to a she-camel, Lean, lank, light of flesh, slender, or lank in the belly: (S, A, K:) or emaciated so that her back has become crooked, or curved. (TA.) ― -b4- [And A^aEowaju applied to a hilaAl (or new moon), Oblique: see A^adofaqu .] ― -b5- naxiylN EuwjN signifies Palm-trees inclining, or leaning, and therefore crooked, or curved: and accord. to some, the saying of Lebeed, describing a [wild] he-ass and his she-asses, waA^aworadahaA EalaY EuwjK TiwaAli [the latter hemistich of a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. Hw* ] means, And he brought them to the watering-place at [ tall ] palm-trees growing over the water, inclining and curving by reason of the abundance of their fruit: but others say that the meaning of ElY Ewj is, upon their crooked legs. (TA.) ― -b6- Hence, EuwjN signifies The legs of a horse or similar beast; (O, TA;) as ISd says, thus used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates [app. implying their having that bending, or curving, and tension of the sinews, termed tajoniyb , agreeably with what here follows]. (TA.) ― -b7- And hence also, (TA,) xayolN EuwjN meaning Horses that have, in their hind legs, the quality termed tajoniyb . (A, TA. *) ― -b8- A^aEowaju applied to a man means [ Crooked in temper, or] evil in natural disposition. (S, A, O, K.) ― -b9- Almil~apu AlEawojaA='u [ The crooked, or perverted, or corrupted, religion ] is a phrase occurring in a trad., applied to the religion of Abraham as changed by the Arabs from its state of rectitude. (TA.) And one says xuT~apN EawojaA='u , and raA^oYN A^aEowaju , meaning [ An affair, and an opinion, ] not of a right kind. (A.) ― -b10- AlA^ay~aAmu EuwjN rawaAjiEu [ The days are apt to decline from the right course, apt to return, ] is a prov., (Meyd, O, TA,) meaning fortune at one time declines from thee, and at another time returns to thee; (Meyd;) said by him at whose affliction one rejoices, or said on his part, and sometimes on an occasion of threatening: Az says that EuwjN , here, may be pl. of A^aEowaju , or of EawojaA='u ; or it may be pl. of ↓ EaAy^ijN , and originally EuwujN . (O, TA.) [Hence,] AlEuwju is used as signifying The days [in allusion to their variableness with respect to good and evil]. (TA.) ― -b11- And A^aEowaju is a [proper] name of A watering-trough. (Th, TA.) ― -b12- See also the next paragraph, in four places.

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaEiyru , He went, or journeyed. (TA.) ― -b2- EaAra fiY AlA^aroDi , aor. as above, He went away in, or into, the land, or country. (S.) ― -b3- And EaAra , (S, O, &c.,) aor. as above, (Msb, K,) inf. n. EiyaArN , (Msb, TA,) or this is a simple subst., (K,) He (a horse, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, and a dog, K) went away (O, K, TA) hither and thither, (O, TA,) which action is also termed muEaAyarapN [inf. n. of ↓ EaAyara ], (O,) as though he had made his escape (K, TA) from his master, going to and fro: (TA:) and the same is said of news: (IKtt, TA:) or escaped, or got loose, and went away hither and thither, by reason of his exceeding sprightliness: (S:) or escaped, or got loose, and went away at random: (Msb:) or went away hither and thither, by reason of his sprightliness: or strayed at random, nothing turning him: (Mgh:) or went away at random, far from his master. (TA.) ― -b4- And EaAra , (aor. as above, TA,) He (a man) came and went, (K,) moving to and fro. (TA.) ― -b5- EaAra fiY Alqawomi yaDoribuhumo biAls~ayofi , (S, * TA,) inf. n. EayaraAnN , (TA,) He (a man) went and came among the people, (TA,) or did mischief among them, (S,) smiting them with the sword. (S, * TA.) ― -b6- EaArati AlqaSiydapu (assumed tropical:) The ode became current. (K.) ― -b7- EaAra , (K,) aor. as above, inf. n. EiyaArN and EayaraAnN , (TA,) He (a camel) left his females that were seven months gone with young, and went away to others, (IKtt, L, K,) to cover them. (IKtt, L.) In [some of] the copies of the K, $awolahaA is put in the place of $awolahu , which latter is the reading in the Tahdheeb of IKtt [and in the CK]. (TA.) -A2- EaArahu , aor. yaEiyruhu and yaEuwruhu , (S and K in art. Ewr ,) or the aor. is not used, or it is scarcely ever used, (TA in the same art.,) He, or it, took, and went away with, him, or it: (S and K in the same art.:) or destroyed him, or it. (K and TA in the same art.) See art. Ewr . You say Eirotu vawobahu , I took, or went away with, his garment. (TA.) And it is said in a prov., EayorN EaArahu watiduhu An ass which his peg [to which he was tethered] destroyed [by preventing his escape from wild beasts that attacked him]. (Meyd, TA. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 87.]) -A3- EaArahu , [aor. as above,] also signifies He blamed, or reproached, him; found fault with him; attributed or imputed to him, or charged him with, or accused him of, a vice, or fault, or the like. (S, O, TA.) [See also what next follows.]

EiyaArN ; (S;) and EAwrhA , (S, K,) and Ew~rhA ; (K;) signify the same, (S, K,) He measured, or compared, the measures of capacity, (Mgh, K,) and the instruments for weighing, one by, or with, another. (Mgh.) One should not say ↓ Ey~r . (S.) The saying AisotaEaAra SanajaAtihi bihaA ↓ daraAhima liyuEay~ira , meaning, [ He borrowed pieces of money ] that he might equalize [ with them the weights of his balance ], should be, correctly, liyuEaAyira . [But in the TA, AlmyzAn ↓ Ey~r and AlmkyAl is mentioned without any remark of disapproval, with EAwrhmA and EAyrhmA .] You also say EAyr bayonahumaA , inf. n. muEaAyarapN and EiyaArN , He measured, or compared, them two. each by, or with, the other, and examined what [ difference ] was between them. (K in art. Ewr .) ― -b2- [Hence, EAyr app. signifies also He assayed gold &c.] -A2- See also 1, third sentence.

sourceDefinition: The ass; (S, O, Msb, K;) both the wild and the domestic; (S, O, Msb;) its predominant application is to the former: (K:) so called because he goes away hither and thither ( yaEiyru fayatarad~adu ) in the desert: (TA:) fem. with p : (S, Msb:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoyaArN , (S, O, Msb, K.) and [of mult.] EiyaArN and EuyuwrN (K) and EuyuwrapN (S, O, Msb, K) and EiyarapN (O) and ↓ maEoyuwraA='u , (S, O, K,) like ma$oyuwxaA='u &c., or this is [properly speaking] a quasi-pl. n., (TA,) and ↓ maEoyuwraY , [also a quasipl. n.,] (Az, TA,) and pl. pl. EiyaraAtN (O) and EiyaAraAtN . (K.) [Dim. EuyayorN , q. v. intra.] ― -b2- It is said in a prov., relating to contentment with that which is present and forgetting what is absent, A_ino *ahaba AlEayoru faEayorN fiY Alr~ibaATi [ If the ass has gone away, there is an ass in the tether ]. (A 'Obeyd.) ― -b3- You say also, of a place in which is no good, huwa kajawofi EayorK [ It is like the belly of an ass ], (S, TA,) or kjwf AlEayori [ like the belly of the ass ]; (TA;) because there is nothing in his belly of which any use is made: (S, TA:) or this originated from the saying huwa A^axolaY mino jawofi HimaArK [ It is more empty than the valley of Himar ]; (S, O, * TA;) for HmAr was the name of a certain unbeliever, who possessed a valley, which for his infidelity, God rendered waste and unproductive; (O, * TA;) and Imra-el-Keys, (O, TA,) as some say, but correctly Taäbbata-sharrà, (O,) quoting the above-mentioned saying, has substituted AlEyr for HmAr , for the sake of the metre. (O, TA.) ― -b4- One says also A^a*al~u mina AlEayori More vile than the ass. (TA.) [But this is doubtful: see the same phrase expl. differently later in this paragraph. The wild ass is superior to every other kind of animal that is an object of the chase: (see faraA^N :) and hence, app., the signification here next following.] ― -b5- EayorN also signifies A lord, or chief, (S, O, K,) of a people: (S, O:) a king: (K:) pl. A^aEoyaArN . (O.) ― -b6- The saying (S, K) of the people of Syria, used by them proverbially, (TA,) EayorN biEayorK waziyaAdapu Ea$arapK [ A lord for a lord, or a lord is succeeded by a lord, and an increase of ten ] is expl. by the fact that, when the Khaleefeh of the sons of Umeiyeh died, and another arose, he increased their stipends by ten dirhems: (S, O, K:) so they said thus on that occasion. (O, TA.) ― -b7- Eayoru Als~araApi is an appellation of A certain bird, (S, O, K, TA,) resembling the pigeon, (S, O, TA,) short in the legs, which are coved with feathers, yellow in the legs and bill, having the eye bordered with black, of a clear colour inclining to greenness, or dark dust-colour, ( xuDorap ,) yellow in the belly and the part beneath its wings and the inner part of its tail; as though it were a variegated burod : pl. Euyuwru Als~araApi : Als~araApu being a place in the district of Et-Táïf: they assert that this bird eats three hundred figs, from the time of their coming forth from among the leaves, small; and in like manner, grapes. (TA.) -A2- Also The prominence, or ridge, in the middle of the iron head or blade of an arrow or of a spear or of a sword or of a knife or the like. (S, O.) [See *ubaAbN .] ― -b2- The prominent line, (S, O, TA,) like a little wall, (TA,) in the middle of a leaf; its middle rib. (S, O, TA.) ― -b3- The spine, i. e. the prominent part, in the middle of the scapula, or shoulderblade. (S, O.) ― -b4- The prominent, or projecting, bone in the middle of the hand: pl. A^aEoyaArN . (TA.) [In the K, it is expl. simply by AlEaZomu Aln~aAtiy^u wasaTahaA : but this is a wrong reading, app. occasioned by an omission, which is supplied in the TA, though somewhat awkwardly: it seems that we should read wamina Alkaf~i AlEaZomu Aln~atiy^u wasaTahaA ; or, more probably, wmn Alkatifi Alx ; for I incline to think that Alkf~ in the TA is a mistake for Alktf , and that the last signification of Eyr , given here, is doubtful.] ― -b5- The prominence, or protuberance, in the upper, or convex, part, or back, of the foot. (S, O, TA.) ― -b6- Any prominent, or protuberant, bone in the body. (TA.) ― -b7- An edge, or a ridge, of a rock, naturally prominent. (TA.) ― -b8- Anything prominent, or protuberant, in an even thing, (K,) or in the middle of an even thing [or surface ]. (TA.) ― -b9- Each of the two portions of flesh and sinew next the back bone, one on either side thereof: both together are called EayoraAni . (K, * TA.) [So called because it forms a kind of ridge.] ― -b10- The prominent, or protuberant, part at the pupil ( buw^obuw^ ) of the eye: (AA, TA:) or the lid of the eye: (S, O, K:) or the inner angle [for maA^`qiY , in the CK, I read maA^oqaY , as in other copies of the K,] of the eye: (Th, K:) or the image that is seen in the black of the eye when a thing faces it; (Aboo-Tálib, L, K; *) also called luEobapN : (Aboo-Tálib, L:) or the eye-ball: (TA:) or a looking from the outer angle ( laHoZ [or perhaps this signifies here the outer angle itself ]) of the eye. (K.) Hence the saying, (S, O,) faEalotu *aAka qabola EayorK wamaA jaraY I did that before a look from the outer angle of the eye: (S, O, K: *) or before he winked [or could wink ]; Eyr meaning the “ image that is seen in the black of the eye; ” and mA jrY , “ what moved, ” i. e., “ the eye itself: ” (Aboo-Tálib:) or before I looked [or could look ] at thee; not used with a negative: (Th:) nor do you say A^afoEalu *Ak [instead of fElt *Ak in this phrase]: (A O, S:) or Eyr here signifies the wild ass. (Lh.) You say also A^atayotuka qabola EayorK wamaA jaraY , meaning I came to thee before a sleeper awoke [or could awake ]. (AA, TA.) ― -b11- The watid [or tragus ] which is in the inner part of the ear: (S:) [see watidN :] or the part of the interior of the ear which is below the faroE [or upper portion thereof ], (K,) in a man and in a horse, like the Eayor [ of the head ] of an arrow: (TA:) or the EayoraAni are the matonaAni [app. meaning the two backs, though the word may have some other application in this case,] of the two ears of a horse: pl. EiyaArN . (TA.) -A3- A wooden pin, peg, or stake, which is fixed in the ground or in a wall. (S, O, K.) Hence, as some say, the prov. fulaAnN A^a*al~u mina AlEayori [ Such a one is more vile than the wooden pin, or peg, of a tent &c.]. (TA.) [See another explanation above: and see also ma*al~apN .] Hence also, accord. to some, (TA,) one says, maA A^adoriY A^aY~u mano Daraba AlEayora huwa , meaning I known not what one of mankind is he. (Yaakoob, S, O, K, TA.) And hence too, as some say, the saying of El-Hárith Ibn-Hillizeh, (O, TA,) zaEamuwA A^an~a kul~a mano Daraba AlEayo ra mawaAlK lanaA waA^an~aA AlwalaA='u of which Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà said that he had passed away, or died, who knew the meaning of this verse, (S, O, TA,) and which is differently related, some saying mawaAlK lahaA , and some saying AlwilaA='u : (TA:) but various meanings are assigned to AlEyr in this instance; and some expl. it as a proper name: (O, TA:) and some, relating this verse, say AlEiyra [q. v.]: (TA:) [the following explanation of the verse has been given as preferable to others:] They (the Arákim, mentioned two verses before,) have asserted that all who have hunted the wild ass are the sons of our paternal uncles, and that we are the relations of them; AlwlA=' being for A^aSoHaAbu walaAy^ihimo : meaning that we are responsible for their crimes, or offences, as though we were their heirs. (EM p. 261.) -A4- Also A certain piece of wood which is in the fore part of the [ vehicle called ] hawodaj . (O, K.) -A5- And A drum. (O, K.) And so, as some say, in the verse cited above. (O, TA.) -A6- And A mountain. (K.) And also the name of A mountain of El-Medeeneh: (K, TA:) and, as some say, of a mountain of Mekkeh. (TA.) -A7- And AlA^aEoyaAru (of which the sing. is AlEayoru , TA) is a name of Certain bright stars in the track of the feet of suhayol [or Canopus ]. (O, K.)

sourceDefinition: A caravan; syn. qaAfilapN ; of the fem. gen.: (K:) from EaAra “ he journeyed: ” (TA:) or camels that carry provision of corn: (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) then generally applied to any caravan: (Mgh, Msb:) or a caravan of asses; and then extended to any caravan; as though pl. of EayorN , being originally and regularly of the measure fuEulN , [i. e. EuyurN ,] like suqufN as pl. of saqofN ; (TA;) but it has no proper sing.: (K:) or any beasts upon which provision of corn is brought, whether camels or asses or mules: (K:) the Eyr mentioned in the Kur xii. 94 consisted of asses; and the assertion of him who says that Eyr is applied specially to camels is false: (AHeyth, O, TA:) Nuseyr cites the poet Aboo-'Amr El-Asadee as applying this appellation to asses; and says that camels are not so called unless employed for bringing provision of corn: (AHeyth, TA:) IAar says that it is applied to camels bearing burdens, and not bearing burdens: (Az:) but camels are not thus called that bring corn for their owners: (TA, voce rikaAb :) pl. EiyaraAtN , (O, K,) with A and t because it is of the fem. gender, and, being a subst., with the Y movent, accord. to the dial. of Hudheyl, for they say jawozaAtN and bayoDaAtN ; (Sb;) and EiyoraAtN (S, K) is allowable, (S,) and is the regular form, and occurs in a trad., meaning horses or the like, and camels carrying merchandise. definition: That goes to and fro, and round about;
sourceDefinition: That goes to and fro, and round about; as also ↓ Eay~aArN : both are applied [to a man and] also to a dog: (TA:) and ↓ the latter is also expl. as follows: a man (TA) often coming and going (K, TA) in the land: (TA:) often going round about, (Fr, S, Msb, K,) often in motion, (Fr, S, Msb,) and sharp, or quick, of intellect: (S, K:) it is used as an epithet of praise and as one of dispraise: for instance, applied to a boy, it signifies brisk in obeying God, and brisk in acts of disobedience: (IAar:) and ↓ Eay~irN , applied to a horse, signifies brisk, lively, or sprightly: (IAar:) and ↓ Eay~aArN , so applied, mischievous; and that is brisk, lively, or sprightly, so that he goes on one side of the way, and then turns to the other side: (TA:) and, applied to a man, that goes to and fro without work: (Ajnás en-Nátifee, Mgh:) or that leaves himself to follow his natural desire, not restraining himself. (IAmb, Mgh, Msb.) It is said in a prov., kalobN EaAy^irN xayorN mino A^asadK raAbiDK A dog going to and fro and round about is better [as a guard] than a lion lying down. (TA.) You say also $aApN EaAy^irapN A sheep that goes to and fro between two flocks, not knowing which of them to follow: to such is a hypocrite likened. (TA.) And naAqapN EaAy^irapN A she-camel that goes forth from the other camels in order that the stallion may cover her (S, O, TA.) And jamalN EaAy^irN A he-camel that leaves the females seven months gone with young, and goes to others. (S.) And bA^awoSaAlK ↓ Eay~aArN A horse that goes away hither and thither, by reason of his sprightliness: (S, O:) or a lion that goes away with the joints, or whole bones. of men to his thicket. (IB.) ↓ AlEay~aAru is an appellation given to The lion, (S, O, K,) because of his coming and going in search of his prey. (S, O.) ― -b2- qaSiydapN EaAy^irapN (assumed tropical:) An ode having currency. (O.) ― -b3- sahomN An arrow from an unknown shouter. (Msb. [Mentioned also in art. Ewr .]) And vamarapN EaAy^irapN A fallen fruit, of which the owner is not known (TA.) -A2- EaAy^iru AlEayoni , and EaAy^irapu EayonK or Eayonayoni , &c.: see art. Ewr .

definition: A thing from which one is unable to free himself, [ a thing ] such as cleaves fast.
sourceDefinition: A thing from which one is unable to free himself, [ a thing ] such as cleaves fast. (BA and Jel in xxv. 66.) Lasting evil. (IAar, S, K.) Perdition: (K:) in the Kur xxv. 66, (S, Ksh,) accord. to AO, (S,) it means perdition, (S, Ksh,) persistent, (Ksh,) and such as cleaves fast. (S, Ksh.) And Punishment, or torment; (S, K) or, accord. to Zj, the most vehement punishment or torment; and accord to Er-Rághib, hardship, or difficulty, and an affliction, or a calamity or misfortune, that befalls a man. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Eager desire [ bi$aYo'K for a thing ]; fondness [for it]; or attachment [to it]; syn. waluwEN : (S, K:) or love that torments the heart. (Har p. 36.) [See 4, last sentence.]

definition: A debtor; (S, Msb, K:) one says, xu*o mino gariymi Als~awo'i maA sabaHa Take thou from the evil debtor what has become easy of attachment, (S:) and ↓ gaArimN signifies the same as gariymN ; or one...
sourceDefinition: A debtor; (S, Msb, K:) one says, xu*o mino gariymi Als~awo'i maA sabaHa Take thou from the evil debtor what has become easy of attachment, (S:) and ↓ gaArimN signifies the same as gariymN ; or one upon whom lies the obligation of a bloodwit or the like; or [it virtually signifies thus, but properly] it is a possessive epithet signifying *uw garaAmK or garaAmapK or tagoriymK . (TA.) And (sometimes, S) it signifies A creditor also: (S, Msb, K:) thus having two contr. meanings; (K) Kutheiyir says, * qaDaY kul~u *iY dayonK fawaf~aY gariymahu * waEaz~apu mamoTuwlN muEan~FY gariymuhaA [ Every debtor has paid, and fully rendered to his creditor; but as to 'Azzeh, her creditor is put off, and wearied ]. (S.) The pl. of gariymN is guramaA='u (I Ath, Msb, TA) and gur~aAmN , which is a strange [i. e. an anomalous] pl., (I Ath, TA;) or this is pl. of ↓ gaArimN as syn. with gariymN [and thus is agree able with analogy]; or it is pl. of ↓ mugorimN [signifying “ burdened with debt. ”], formed by the rejection of the augmentative letter [of the sing]. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, An adversary in contention, dispute, or litigation; an antagonist; a litigant; because, by his pressing upon his adversary [like the creditor upon his debtor], he becomes one who cleaves, or clings. (Msb.)
